   needs its working directory moved. Mike would almost never claim this way,
   but another user might, and it should work rather than fail.

2. Claim ran from a shell, no tmux. Refuse: tmux is required.

3. Claim ran from a shell inside a tmux window holding one pane. Do the work:
   split the window into two sibling PANES — horizontal running `esm`
   (`endless session monitor`), vertical running nothing. Confirmed by Mike.

4. Claim resolved a Claude session in a SIBLING pane. Refuse and say to run
   `session goto --resume` instead. Deliberately not handled: covering it means
   deciding what happens to every other pane and window in play, and tmux panes
   are cheap enough that the complexity is not worth the benefit.

5. `--unattended`. E-2093 split `claim --force`, which used to spell two
   unrelated decisions; this is the half meaning "claim with NO Claude session
   bound". Without it, a claim from a plain shell with no Claude anywhere is
   refused. With it, the task is claimed and `sessions.task_id` is left unset.
   So there is no session to route to and no resume to offer: print the worktree
   and stop.

   The NAME is wrong and Mike flagged it. "Unattended" describes automation
   running unsupervised, but the flag's primary use is a HUMAN working by hand
   at a terminal — very much attended. What is absent is a bound Claude session,
   not a person. It is also one letter of intent away from the global
   `--no-session`, which governs event ATTRIBUTION rather than binding, and
   claim's own docstring already spends a paragraph warning the two apart.
   Rename it to name what is absent — `--unbound` or `--no-bind`. Out of scope
   here; file separately if wanted.

Verify by claiming a task whose worktree already exists from each of the five
callers above, and by pointing both resume paths at a session whose transcript
file has been removed.

Settled design, from working through it with Mike. Part 2 of the original
description is already done: ED-1073 was widened the same morning E-1934 was
filed and now reads "no time-frozen specifics in any durable field", enumerating
description, analysis, text/plan, outcome and decision bodies. What remains is
the gate (part 1) and the guide wording (part 3).

## Rule 3 — line citations

`_guard_inline_content` has Rule 1 (whole value is a path token) and Rule 2 (an
absolute path token anywhere). Rule 3 refuses a line citation.

- Matches `<name>.<ext>:<digits>` where `<ext>` is in the citation-extension
  set. Also `<name>.<ext>:<digits>-<digits>` (range) and
  `<name>.<ext>:<digits>:<digits>` (line:col).
- Does NOT match a bare leading-colon number. Nobody writes a bare line number
  that way, and the false positives are everywhere: clock times, host:port,
  ratios.
- Skips any token preceded by a scheme separator or an at-sign, or beginning
  with a www prefix. This is what keeps host:port out of the gate, and it is
  load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces: many source extensions ARE ccTLDs
  (Serbia, Paraguay, Poland, Saint Helena, Mali, Cocos, Moldova), so the
  extension set alone does not separate a file citation from a domain.
- No escape hatch. Rule 2 has one; Rule 3 does not.
- Applies wherever Rule 2 applies: description, text/plan, analysis, outcome and
  decision bodies. E-1992 collapses these into task_content, at which point the
  gate stops enumerating flags and guards content.

## Configuration

Three keys under a content block in the project config file, which already
carries list-valued keys, so no new shape is needed.

- A built-in default extension set of roughly eighty entries covering systems,
  JVM and .NET, scripting, JS/TS and web, functional, data and config, docs,
  and build and schema files.
- Two thin override lists layered over that default rather than replacing it,
  so a project adding or removing one extension does not restate eighty. Named
  `content.extensions.block` and `content.extensions.unblock`, nested. The verb
  attaches to the behaviour rather than to set membership, which is what makes
  it readable a year later: block names one more extension whose citations are
  refused, unblock stops refusing one the default covers. Earlier candidates
  spelled around an abstract "set the gate matches" and every one of them was
  ambiguous in one direction or the other.
- An extension listed in BOTH lists is a config error and must be refused at
  load, not silently resolved. That follows the house pattern already set by
  --clear against a field flag, and by --status against --keep-status: when two
  settings spell contradictory intent, refuse and say so.
- A switch that disables the gate outright, for a project that finds it more
  trouble than it is worth, nested alongside as `content.extensions` sits under
  `content`. Worth giving Rule 2 its own switch at the same time, by the same
  reasoning.

## Widening the built-in path exemption

`_builtin_allowed_dirs` exempts endless's own config and cache directories, and
its docstring already anticipates being extended at that composition point.
Widen it to any dot-directory directly under home. Rule 2's stated rationale is
that absolute paths are non-portable and that a temp path dies with the
worktree; neither is true of a tool's conventional dot-directory under home,
which names the same location for every user on every machine. Home-relative
paths that are NOT dot-directories stay refused — a personal projects directory
really is machine-specific. Encountered live: writing a lesson about the Claude
transcript directory was refused, and the text had to be degraded to prose that
named no location.

## Part 3 — guide wording

The tasks guide still describes text as a full implementation plan "including
approach, file paths, verification steps", which invites the thing ED-1073
forbids, and says nothing about line numbers anywhere. Fix the wording to say
file and function names.

fields.title: Wire the Notification hook and record when a session is waiting on the user
fields.description: Endless never wired Claude Code's Notification hook, so it cannot see a session paused on a permission prompt — that session reads 'working', indistinguishable from one doing work. E-1976 built the display side and left the producer out: its board's first rank has none. Install the hook, add a 'prompted' state to internal/sessionstate classified into all five groups (MayWrite included, so approving a prompt never leaves the session refused), route notification_type permission_prompt to it and idle_prompt to idle, and clear it on the session's next activity. Waiting on the user means the session paused for input, question or not, so AwaitsHuman becomes the one place that answers it. Also stops InitSession and the revive CASE from writing needs_input, and reveals those rows on the board instead of hiding them.
fields.text:
# Plan — record when a session is waiting on the user

Blocked by E-2105, which gives the session state vocabulary an owning package.
Every step assumes `internal/sessionstate` exists and that Python reads the
vocabulary from it rather than holding a copy.

## 1. Install the hook

Add `Notification` to `CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENTS` in `src/endless/setup.py`.

NOT in `SYNC_EVENTS`: the handler records a state and gates nothing, so it has no
reason to block the harness. Every member of that set is there because something
downstream reads what it wrote within the same turn.

Existing installs need nothing extra. `_repair_missing_hook_events` already adds
an endless-go entry for any hooked event that has none, precisely so a machine
whose install predates an event still gains it — verified, not assumed.

## 2. The state

Add `Prompted` to `internal/sessionstate` and classify it into all five groups,
which the package makes unskippable:

| Group          | Member? | Why |
|----------------|---------|-----|
| `All`          | yes     | `working, prompted, idle, needs_input, ended` — lifecycle order; beside `working` because it is a mid-turn state |
| `Live`         | yes     | the session is running |
| `MayWrite`     | **yes** | decided 2026-09-01; see the analysis |
| `AwaitsHuman`  | yes     | it is the definition of the group |
| `DisplayOrder` | first   | `prompted, working, needs_input, idle, ended` |

Label `prompted`. Glyph the warning sign E-1976's board already uses for the
rank; it measures one column under go-runewidth, which the vocabulary's glyph
test asserts for every member.

Transition rows: `any -> prompted` (Notification / `monitor.PromptSession`) and
`prompted -> working` (see §4).

`AwaitsHuman` is the group that carries this task's definition of waiting: after
this change it holds `idle`, `needs_input` and `prompted` — every state in which
the session has paused for the user, question or no question. Anything that needs
to ask "is this session waiting on me" asks that group, not a list of states.

## 3. The handler

`case "Notification":` in `internal/hookcmd/claude.go`, reading the payload's
`notification_type` field and acting on exactly two values:

- `permission_prompt` -> `monitor.PromptSession(sessionID)`, a new helper beside
  `IdleSession`/`EndSession` writing the `prompted` state and refreshing
  `last_activity`.
- `idle_prompt` -> `monitor.IdleSession(sessionID)`. It means the input prompt
  sat untouched for 60 seconds, which is what `idle` already says. Idempotent on
  a session already idle.

Every other value writes no state. `notification_type` carries at least a dozen
documented values — auth, elicitation, quota, agent-team — and a notification
Endless does not model must not move the session. An unrecognised value is also
the shape a harness change arrives in.

`claudePayload` gains `NotificationType string` with the `notification_type` tag.

`monitor.ParseTranscript` is NOT called here: Notification is not a turn boundary
and carries no new messages.

## 4. Clearing it

`prompted` returns to `working` on the session's next activity, via
`monitor.ResumeFromPrompt(sessionID)` which updates only when the current state
is `prompted`, so it can never demote a session that moved on another way.

Called from `PostToolUse` (the approved tool completed) and `UserPromptSubmit`
(the user typed instead). `Stop` needs no change: it writes `idle`
unconditionally, correct for a turn that ended with a prompt outstanding.

Deliberately NOT folded into `TouchSession`, which never clobbers a live state;
making it the exception for one value is how a general helper starts carrying
special cases.

Because `prompted` is in `MayWrite`, a missed clear costs a stale glyph until the
next Stop. It cannot refuse anyone.

## 5. Stop making new `needs_input` sediment

`monitor.InitSession` writes `needs_input` as a row's initial value, and the
revive-an-ended-row CASE (`monitor.TouchSession`, `internal/events/executor.go`)
writes it on any incoming hook. Neither means a person is being waited on.

Both become `idle`, which is what they actually mean: the session exists and is
not doing anything. `needs_input` is then written by nothing, and means only what
the declaration gate says.

The 34 existing rows are NOT migrated. They are surfaced by §6 so they can be
resolved deliberately; retiring them automatically is the opposite of what
revealing them is for.

## 6. Reveal them on the board

`internal/monitor/project_status.go`: `boardSessionStates` is deleted, and the
session query filters on `sessionstate.SQLList(sessionstate.Live)`. E-1976's
exclusion of `needs_input` goes with it, along with its comment.

`internal/projectstatuscmd/board.go`: `classify()` routes `prompted` to
`actWaiting`, alongside the existing `needs_input` arm. Both are waiting on the
user; the board's age column already distinguishes a live prompt from a
two-month-old row on sight, which is what that column is for.

## 7. What this does NOT change

The board's RANK ORDER. `idle` sits sixth of seven today, which under this
task's definition of waiting is arguably too low — but that is a display
question, and the board's UI is being reshaped separately. Recognising state and
displaying it are orthogonal; this task does the first, completely, and leaves
the second alone so the redesign is not pre-empted.

No classification of how a turn ended, no reading of the final assistant message,
and no dependency on the minimizer, which is disabled and out of this task's
critical path by decision.

## 8. Python

None, if E-2105 landed as planned: the `--state` choice and the glyph map both
come from the registry, so `prompted` flows through. Verify rather than assume —
`endless session list --state prompted` must be accepted and must render the
warning glyph.

## 9. Migration

None. No row carries `prompted` today and no existing value changes meaning.

## 10. Verification

`.endless/tasks/e-2091/verify.sh`, sourcing `_harness.sh`:

1. Fail-fast unit gate: `internal/sessionstate`, `internal/hookcmd`,
   `internal/monitor`, `internal/projectstatuscmd`, and the Python suite.
2. `Prompted` is in `MayWrite` — asserted directly, because it is the decision
   the design turns on and its absence is a wedged session, not a wrong glyph.
3. The declaration gate admits a prompted session: drive `sessionMayWrite` with
   a prompted session holding a task and assert it may write.
4. `AwaitsHuman` holds `idle`, `needs_input` and `prompted` — the vocabulary's
   statement of what waiting means, pinned so a later edit is deliberate.
5. State machine round trip: `PromptSession` then `ResumeFromPrompt` yields
   `working`; `ResumeFromPrompt` on a working session is a no-op; `Stop` from
   `prompted` yields `idle`.
6. The handler routes `permission_prompt` and `idle_prompt` and IGNORES a third
   value, asserted against synthetic payloads rather than a live harness.
7. No writer produces `needs_input`: a sweep asserting `InitSession` and the
   revive CASE write `idle`, plus a seeded SessionStart landing on `idle`.
8. `setup.py` installs seven events with `Notification` among them and not in
   `SYNC_EVENTS`, and a settings file carrying only the old six is repaired to
   seven rather than reported correct.
9. End to end against a seeded throwaway database: a prompted session renders as
   the board's first row, and a `needs_input` session renders rather than being
   suppressed.
fields.analysis:
## What is missing

Endless installs six Claude Code hooks — PreToolUse, SessionStart,
UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd. None reports that Claude Code is
asking the user for permission, so a session sitting on a prompt reads `working`,
indistinguishable from one doing work. `Notification` is the event that reports
it and was never wired.

E-1976 built the display side and left the producer out: `actWaiting` is the
board's first rank, wears the warning glyph, renders bold, and `classify()`
already routes a state to it. The rank has no producer. That is this task.

## What "waiting on the user" means here

Decided with Mike (2026-09-03): a session is waiting on the user whenever it has
paused for input, whether or not it asked a question. A finished turn and a
question are the same thing for this purpose — the ball is in the user's court —
which is exactly what his tmux window flag already signals and has proven
accurate in practice.

That definition is what keeps the task small. There is no question-versus-
finished classification, no inspection of the turn's final message, and no model
call. `idle` already means "the turn ended", so the work is to add the one
paused-for-input case Endless cannot currently see — a permission prompt — and to
make the vocabulary say that both are the same kind of waiting.

Explicitly not coupled to the minimizer. It is disabled until further notice,
will be renamed when it returns, and nothing on this task's critical path may
depend on it.

## What the current hooks reference says

Checked against the live documentation rather than recall, which was two months
and twenty-four events out of date.

Claude Code exposes 33 hook events. `Notification` carries a `notification_type`
field whose documented values include `permission_prompt` and `idle_prompt`.

Two findings that shaped the design:

- `agent_needs_input` exists but is scoped to agent-team teammates about to go
  idle, alongside a `TeammateIdle` event. It is NOT a main-session "the agent
  asked you something" signal, and designing on it would have been wrong.
- `PermissionRequest` is now a first-class event carrying `tool_name`,
  `tool_input` and `tool_use_id`. It is nevertheless the wrong signal for this
  task: it fires whenever a permission DECISION is needed, which an allowlist or
  another hook can resolve without the user ever seeing anything.
  `Notification` with `permission_prompt` fires when the user is actually
  prompted, which is the fact this task records.

## Why a new state rather than `needs_input`

`needs_input` looks like the obvious home and is not. It is ENFORCED:
`hookcmd.sessionMayWrite` refuses file writes from a session in that state under
`enforce` tracking, with the message "you asked your user something and the
answer has not arrived. There is no command for you to run."

That state means the AGENT asked the USER something. A permission prompt is the
reverse — the agent is trying to act and the harness is asking — and routing one
to the other would refuse the session's next write after the user approved.

The near miss is worth recording because it was not carelessness. The gate's
admission set was a Go `switch` with a silent `default: return false`, so a new
state joined the refused set without anyone deciding it should. That is why
E-2105 came first: with `MayWrite` a named group, a state cannot be added
without the question being answered.

## Why `prompted` may write

Decided with Mike (2026-09-01), from the gate's own stated rule rather than from
preference. The gate admits a session that "has DECLARED what it is working on
and is live-and-acting", and already glosses `idle` as admissible because "a
write from an idle session is by definition mid-turn". A prompt-blocked session
is mid-turn by exactly that reasoning, and the tool it waits on is its own.

The decisive argument was the asymmetry of failure modes. Both readings need a
clearing transition. If the clear misses under this one, a stale glyph sits on
the board until the next Stop — cosmetic, self-correcting. If it missed under the
other, every prompted session would be refused its next write and told there is
no command to run, which is the failure E-2093 was cleaning up after.

## The `needs_input` writers are the real defect underneath

Two writers put `needs_input` in the database and neither means a person is being
waited on: `monitor.InitSession` writes it as a row's initial value at
SessionStart, and the revive-an-ended-row CASE writes it on any incoming hook
(E-1686). Nothing else writes it.

Measured while E-1976 was built: 34 rows in `endless` carrying it, every one last
active 25 to 71 days earlier, none on a pane that still existed — sessions that
registered and never had a turn.

E-1976 responded by excluding the state from the board. Mike's correction
(2026-09-03): that is backwards. Hiding them is how they rotted unseen, the board
already caps each rank at ten rows with a footer naming the remainder — machinery
built for exactly this — and revealing them is what provides the mechanism to
resolve them.

So this task reveals the rows and fixes the writers, and deliberately does not
retire the existing 34. They are surfaced to be dealt with, not migrated away in
the dark. Once drained, `needs_input` has no writer and no rows, and means only
what the declaration gate says it means.

payload.title: Explore what an Endless session is without Claude and without tmux
payload.description: Endless assumes Claude and tmux so foundationally that the agent-less path is barely designed: claim --unattended claims a task and leaves sessions.task_id unset, so the work has no session record and no route back. If a session record is the spine, then what is absent in that case is an AGENT, not a session — which argues the flag should be --no-agent and should still mint a session, and raises the question of what a non-Claude session row holds and how it starts and ends. Map what breaks without tmux (goto, resume, monitor, status line) and without Claude (transcripts, hooks, handoff, spawn) before changing anything. Expect a follow-up research task. The --unattended rename rides along rather than landing first, since renaming a flag before deciding whether the concept survives is churn.

triage.rationale: The description explicitly frames this as exploratory mapping work with an expected follow-up research task, leaving the session schema, flag rename, and start/end semantics for non-Claude/non-tmux sessions undecided.

fields.analysis:
Endless resolves a resume target out of `sessions.session_id` and hands the UUID
to `claude --resume` without ever checking that the transcript still exists, so
a session whose transcript is gone fails differently at each entry point and
never routes the user anywhere. Found while trying to pick E-1934 back up: its
claiming session ended after thirty seconds and its transcript is absent from
disk and from every Time Machine backup taken after it ran.

(a) `session goto <ref> --resume` appears to do nothing. `_open_resume_window`
passes the `claude --resume` command line to `tmux new-window`, which succeeds
because the window really was created, so Endless reports `(new window)` and
returns a pane id. The claude process inside then exits on the missing
transcript and the window closes. No error reaches the caller.

(b) `session resume <ref>` reports only Claude's own error. `resume_session`
execs `claude --resume` directly, so nothing says what Endless resolved or what
to do instead. `--dry-run` against the same ref resolves cleanly and prints a
worktree, which makes the failure look unrelated to the transcript.

Both should stat the transcript before launching and refuse with a route rather
than a dead end. The route exists: a task whose claimant has ended is still
claimable, so a fresh Claude session plus `task claim` picks the work up, and
`task bind` attaches ownership without moving status. Neither is discoverable
from the failure today.

(c) `claim_item` prints a "To work on this task, choose one:" block after every
claim, and both options are wrong for the case that reaches it most often — a
re-claim onto a task whose worktree already exists. Option 1 offers
`task spawn`, which `_check_prior_claim` refuses whenever the task has any prior
claimant, which a re-claim always does. Option 2 spells out `/cd`, `shell-init`
and `eswt`.

## What claim should print instead, by caller

Replace the block with one outcome per caller, decided from how the bound
session resolved. `_resolve_session_id_with_prompt` returns a bare id today and
does not report which layer produced it, so it needs to report provenance —
env/pane, sibling pane, or nothing — before this can branch.

1. Claim ran INSIDE the Claude session being bound (env or direct pane match).
   Print `/cd <worktree>` and nothing else. The session is already here; it only
   needs its working directory moved. Mike would almost never claim this way,
   but another user might, and it should work rather than fail.

2. Claim ran from a shell, no tmux. Refuse: tmux is required.

3. Claim ran from a shell inside a tmux window holding one pane. Do the work:
   split the window into two sibling PANES — horizontal running `esm`
   (`endless session monitor`), vertical running nothing. Confirmed by Mike.

4. Claim resolved a Claude session in a SIBLING pane. Refuse and say to run
   `session goto --resume` instead. Deliberately not handled: covering it means
   deciding what happens to every other pane and window in play, and tmux panes
   are cheap enough that the complexity is not worth the benefit.

5. `--unattended`. Scope here is only the printed line: there is no bound
   Claude session, so there is nothing to resume. Print the worktree and stop.
   Everything else about this flag — whether an agent-less claim should mint a
   session record at all, and whether the flag should be renamed --no-agent —
   is E-2110, deliberately out of scope for this task.

Verify by claiming a task whose worktree already exists from each of the five
callers above, and by pointing both resume paths at a session whose transcript
file has been removed.

payload.title: Decide how to get the exact unlanded answer without paying for it on every tool call
payload.description: E-2087 made 'does this branch hold work the base lacks?' exact via git range-diff, then had to be reverted on the worktree reaper because the reaper runs on PreToolUse/PostToolUse and a ~90s sweep stopped the product. The display surfaces keep the exact answer; the reaper is back to the cheap SHA check and its known leak. Decide how to have both — caching keyed on branch/base tip OIDs, taking the reaper off the hook path, a cheaper exact algorithm, or fixing the landing-recording gap underneath.
payload.analysis:
## The problem

"Does this branch hold work the base branch lacks?" has an exact answer and a
cheap answer, and they are not the same answer.

- **Exact** (E-2087, `unlandedCommits` in internal/monitor/worktree_unlanded.go):
  `git range-diff` between the branch and the base since their merge base.
  Recognises a commit a rebasing land re-hashed, and one whose diff changed when
  a conflict was resolved. Measured cost: ~1-2s per worktree, scaling with how
  far the branch has drifted from the base, NOT with what the branch holds. A
  worktree 2251 commits behind main costs 2.1s on its own.
- **Cheap** (`reapNothingToLand` in internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go):
  `git rev-list --count HEAD ^base ^<recorded landing>...`. One call, ~5ms.
  Cannot see a landing that was not recorded, so it over-reports outstanding
  work — safe for a delete decision, wrong for a display.

## What happened, and why this is filed

E-2087 replaced the SHA check with the exact one everywhere the two shared a
probe — including the worktree reaper. `monitor.ReapWorktreesForProject` is
called from FIVE branches of internal/hookcmd/claude.go, among them PreToolUse
and PostToolUse, so the reaper sweeps every worktree before and after every tool
call in every session. At ~90s per sweep that stopped the product, not just
`task spawn`.

The hotfix reverted the reaper to the cheap check and left the exact one on the
display surfaces (◆ in `session status`, `task unsettled`), which probe one row
or a handful rather than 139. The debt it accepted: a worktree whose work landed
under rewritten SHAs with no `task_landings` row reads as holding work forever,
so its directory is never reclaimed. That is the leak E-1940 and E-2087 each
tried to close, reopened deliberately because a slow leak is survivable and a
90-second tool call is not.

## What to decide

How to have the exact answer without paying for it per tool call. Directions
worth weighing, not a menu to pick from:

1. **Cache the verdict, keyed on (branch tip OID, base tip OID).** Both are
   ~1ms to read, and the key self-invalidates when either ref moves. The
   question is where it lives (a table? a file under the worktree's .git?) and
   what happens after a land, which moves the base and invalidates every entry
   at once — the cold sweep is back to ~90s unless something warms it.
2. **Take the reaper off the hook path.** A destructive background sweep
   running before and after every tool call is questionable independent of what
   it costs. Debounce it, run it on a timer, or move it to session start/end.
   This may be the real fix, with caching a nice-to-have on top.
3. **Make the exact answer cheaper.** The cost is dominated by patch-ids for
   every commit the base gained since the fork. Measured alternatives:
   `git cherry` (patch-id only) is ~3x faster but misses conflict-resolved
   landings; pairing by subject + author date is ~35x faster but disagrees with
   range-diff in BOTH directions, so it is unsafe alone. A union or a two-stage
   filter may be exact enough and much cheaper.
4. **Stop needing it.** ED-1587 makes branch names derivable and retires
   `task_landings.branch`. If landings were also recorded reliably, the cheap
   check would rarely be wrong — E-2087 measured worktrees whose work is on main
   with no landing row at all, and that recording gap is arguably the real
   defect underneath both leaks.

## Constraints any answer has to respect

- The reaper's mistakes are not symmetric. Refusing to reap costs disk; reaping
  a worktree that still holds work destroys it. Whatever it consults must be
  wrong only in the safe direction, or be exact.
- ◆, `task unsettled` and the reaper are supposed to agree about what "landed"
  means. The hotfix broke that on purpose and it should not stay broken.
- Whatever runs on the hook path is paid before and after every tool call.
  Budget it in milliseconds.

payload.title: Fix session resume refusing to self-resume the pane's own current task
payload.description: The guard that blocks session resume <id> when the pane already has a task variable assigned does not short-circuit when the resume target is that SAME task. Resume execs in place to avoid clobbering a different session, but self-resuming the pane current task clobbers nothing. It wrongly forces session goto --resume (new window) or --force. Expected: same-task self-resume proceeds without --force.

triage.rationale: The bug, root cause, and expected fix (short-circuit the guard when resume target equals the pane's current task) are all fully specified.

fields.analysis:
## Repro
In a tmux pane already bound to (working) E-1644, from the worktree:

    $ endless session resume E-1644 --db main
    Error: This pane is working E-1644. `session resume` execs in place, so it would replace that session.
      Open the target in a NEW window instead:
          endless session goto E-1644 --resume
      Or pass --force to replace this pane.

## Problem
`session resume` execs in place, so the guard refuses when the pane already has a task
variable assigned — to avoid clobbering a DIFFERENT live session in that pane. But when the
resume TARGET is the SAME task the pane already owns, there is no other session to protect:
resuming yourself replaces nothing meaningful (it is a re-enter of the task you are already on).
The guard should short-circuit that case instead of forcing `session goto --resume` (a new
window) or `--force`.

## Expected
When the pane's bound task == the resume target, `session resume <id>` proceeds without
`--force` — either a friendly no-op ("already here") or a clean re-enter/resume of the current
task. The replace-guard should fire ONLY when the pane's current task differs from the target.

## Fix location (starting point)
The `session resume` command's ownership/replace guard — the check that prints
"This pane is working E-<id>. `session resume` execs in place, so it would replace that
session." Add an equality short-circuit: if the current pane's bound task == the requested
target, bypass the "would replace that session" refusal. Confirm `session goto` and the
`--force` path stay unaffected.

## Verify
From a pane bound to task X: `endless session resume X` exits 0 (no `--force`) and does NOT
print the replace refusal; `endless session resume Y` (Y != X) still refuses without `--force`.

## Encountered
Hit live in session 6e7f46fb (the E-1644 worktree) on 2026-06-29 while trying to resume this
very task after it was completed.

payload.title: Stop recording a probe fault when git was killed by a signal
payload.description: A git probe killed by a signal is recorded as ERR-0010 worktree-probe-failed, so quitting `session monitor` with Ctrl-C leaves a permanent error incident naming a task that is fine. Observed for E-1972 seconds after a land: `git range-diff: signal: interrupt`, one occurrence, while the probe answers cleanly on demand. E-1940's fail-closed rule cannot tell 'git could not run' from 'git was killed because its parent was interrupted', and treats both as an unverifiable worktree worth an incident.
payload.analysis:
## What was observed

2026-09-06 00:20:03 EDT, thirteen seconds after a land: incident 11,
`E-1972: git range-diff failed for its worktree`, detail
`git range-diff: signal: interrupt`. One occurrence.

The probe is healthy. `endless task unsettled E-1972` answers cleanly on
demand (unlanded, 7 commits), and a genuinely broken probe would not have
one occurrence — `session monitor` re-probes every row every two seconds
and the fault dedupes on (worktree, probe), so a real failure drives the
count into the thousands within a minute. The child git was KILLED, not
failed.

## Mechanism

`monitor.runGit` (internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go) uses a plain
`exec.Command`, so the git child inherits the pane's foreground process
group. Ctrl-C to quit `session monitor` — routine after a land, since the
land replaces the global binary — reaches the in-flight git as well as the
monitor. Process table at the time confirms it: a monitor restarted at
00:19:57 and another at 00:20:04, bracketing the fault.

`worktreeUnsettledAt` (internal/monitor/worktree_unsettled.go) then applies
E-1940's fail-closed rule: any error from the probe means "this worktree
cannot be verified", which marks the row ◆ and calls `recordProbeFault`.
That rule cannot distinguish

  - git could not run (absent, broken repo, permissions) — a real incident, and
  - git was killed because its parent was interrupted — not an incident at all.

so a user quitting a view leaves a permanent error naming an innocent task.

## Fix direction

An `exec.ExitError` whose `ProcessState.Sys().(syscall.WaitStatus)` reports
`Signaled()` is not a probe failure. Return undetermined and record nothing:
the render is being torn down anyway, and nothing is left to display the ◆ to.
SIGINT and SIGTERM are the cases that matter; SIGKILL is ambiguous (an OOM kill
is arguably worth knowing about) and is worth a deliberate decision rather than
being swept in with the rest.

Worth deciding alongside: whether the probe should take a context, so an
interrupt CANCELS the sweep rather than racing it. Today each row's git is
killed independently and the loop keeps going, starting new children as it goes.

## Scope note

The FREQUENCY of this is a property of E-2111's cost problem — with
`git range-diff` on the display path, sampling `ps` once a second for ten
seconds found 4-6 of them in flight at every instant on this machine, so a
Ctrl-C lands on one with near-certainty. That measurement is recorded in
E-2111's analysis.

The misclassification is worth fixing independently of what E-2111 decides.
Any probe can be interrupted, including the cheap ones: making range-diff free
would shrink the window without closing it, and `git status --porcelain` sits
behind the same fail-closed rule.

triage.rationale: it doesn't specify how to distinguish a signal-killed git process from a genuine probe failure (e.g., exit-status/signal check vs. exempting SIGINT specifically) or whether the fix belongs in the probe runner or the fail-closed classifier.

payload.title: Add a verb update command so category, definition and machine-only can be corrected
payload.description: endless verb has add, list and remove but no update, so correcting a verb means remove-then-add: you must retype the definition, restate every --category, and remember whether it was --machine-only, and a mistake in any of the three silently rewrites the verb instead of fixing it. Hit live when 'brainstorm' turned out to be registered as an action verb, which made a brainstorm-type task refuse a title led by the word 'brainstorm'. Add 'verb update <value>' taking --definition, --category (repeatable) and --machine-only, changing only what is passed and leaving the rest as-is.

triage.rationale: The command name, arguments (--definition, --category repeatable, --machine-only), and update-only-what's-passed semantics are all fully specified, mirroring the existing add/list/remove pattern.

fields.analysis:
## Three flags, one candidate name

Two existing flags are in play, they control unrelated machinery, and BOTH are
candidates to be replaced by `--no-agent`. They cannot both take the name, and
deciding that is part of this brainstorm rather than a detail to settle later.

- `claim --unattended` (E-2093) governs BINDING. With it, a task is claimed and
  `sessions.task_id` is left unset, so the work has no session record. Its half
  of the old `claim --force` was "claim with no Claude session bound".
- `--no-session` (E-1444) is GLOBAL, accepted in any position, and governs
  ATTRIBUTION. It sets a module flag the event write layer reads, which
  downgrades `actor.kind` to system and NULLs the envelope's session id. It
  exists, in its own words, for callers with no Claude session to attribute to:
  plain shell, cron, scripts. It does NOT skip session resolution — run it from
  a Claude pane and the claim still binds normally.

## Why the name collides

If the answer to the central question is "a session record always exists, and
what varies is whether an agent drives it", then both flags are misnamed by the
same reasoning, because in both cases the absent thing is the agent.

But the third possibility is more interesting than renaming either: if an
agent-less claim mints a session record, then `--no-session` may not need a new
name because it may not need to exist. Its whole purpose is to have somewhere to
put attribution when there is no session to credit. Give it a session to credit
and events can be attributed to that row instead of downgraded to system, and
the flag collapses rather than being renamed.

So the ordering is: settle whether an agent-less claim mints a session; then see
how many of these two flags survive; then name what is left. Renaming first
would be churn, which is the same reason the rename does not lead this task.

fields.text:
# Plan — E-1934

Design rationale lives in this task's analysis; this is the build order. Part 2
(widen ED-1073) is already done and is not in scope.

## 1. The predicate

New helper beside the existing path helpers in the CLI module, next to
`_is_absolute_path`, `_is_path_shaped` and `_absolute_path_tokens`. It returns
the offending tokens in content, matching:

- `<name>.<ext>:<digits>` where `<ext>` is in the effective extension set
- the same with a range suffix (`-<digits>`)
- the same with a column suffix (`:<digits>`)

It skips any token preceded by a scheme separator or an at-sign, or beginning
with a www prefix, so a host and port is never mistaken for a citation. That
guard is load-bearing, not decoration: many source extensions are also ccTLDs.

It does NOT match a bare leading-colon number.

## 2. Where it runs

In `_resolve_content_flag`, on the RESOLVED content — both the inline branch and
the file branch — not inside `_guard_inline_content`.

This is the one structural decision in the task. `_guard_inline_content` sees
inline values only; the resolver's own docstring says file content "is otherwise
trusted and never gated". A plan citing line numbers throughout is exactly the
thing E-1934 exists to stop, and a plan is long-form, so it arrives by

# E-2095 — Plan

Make it visible whether a task's work is on main, and whether its record is
still authoritative. Four parts, one problem: a reader cannot see the facts that
decide whether to trust a row.

## Scope

**In:** parts 1, 2, 4, 5 of the analysis, plus a data-repair pass (§6).

**Out:** part 3 (record supersession automatically when an excision deletes
another task's landed files). It is blocked on a recording change that does not
exist: `task_landings` stores a merge SHA but no base, so a landing's commit
range cannot be reconstructed, and `task_files` stopped recording 2026-07-11.
Its full spec stays in this task's `--analysis`; file a successor when the
recording change is actually wanted rather than parking a speculative task in
the backlog (ED-1550 rule 1).

**Depends on E-2087**, which has landed. It shipped the content-based probe this
task consumes — do not write a second one.

## Decisions already taken (do not relitigate)

- Landedness is measured by CONTENT, not SHA. E-2087's `unlandedCommits`
  short-circuits on `countRevs` when HEAD is an ancestor of base, and only then
  runs `git range-diff`. Reuse it; never reach for `git cherry`.
- No date-scoped filter anywhere. An earlier draft proposed excluding tasks
  created before the project's first landing record. That is Endless's own
  biography, not product behaviour, and it would have hidden real unlanded work.
  §2's two sections replace it.
- New verb, not a flag. `task landed --not-on-main` reads as a contradiction.
- Part 4's banner follows E-2097's shipped shape exactly.

---

## 1. `task show` states landedness instead of implying it

Today the `Landed:` line renders only when a `task_landings` row exists, so
"landed before landings were recorded" and "the branch still holds the work"
both render as nothing. Absence is doing work it cannot do.

For a task in a terminal status, always render a landing line, one of:

- `Landed: <ts> <sha>` — a landing row exists. Unchanged from today.
- `Landed: never — no landing recorded` — no row, and no branch, or a branch
  holding nothing main lacks.
- `Landed: never — branch <branch> holds N commits not on main` — no row and
  the probe reports outstanding commits.

Cost: the third case needs the probe, the first two do not. E-2087's
short-circuit makes the common case a `rev-list --count`; only a branch that
genuinely differs pays for `range-diff`. Do NOT add an opt-in flag to request
the probe — an opt-in probe is one nobody remembers to pass.

Edge cases that must render distinctly rather than collapsing into "clean":

- **No branch** (reaped, or never created). The probe cannot run. Say "no
  landing recorded", never "nothing outstanding".
- **Probe failure.** `unlandedCommits` returns a `gitProbeError` naming the git
  command. Surface that, do not swallow it into a clean reading.
- **Uncommitted changes are a different axis** and belong to `task unsettled`.
  This line reports commits only.

## 2. `endless task unlanded`

A sibling verb to `task landed`, sharing one implementation.

**Wiring.** Put the query in `task_cmd.py` beside `landed_list`, and register
two Click commands that differ only in the mode they pass. Bundle the shared
options with a decorator the way `rowcap.limit_options_for` already does — its
own docstring gives the reason: "One factory so the two flags cannot appear on
one command and not another, and so their help text is written once." E-967's
`task_cmd.add_command(task_show, name="detail")` is the precedent for a second
name over one callback. Nothing is duplicated; there is no Click obstacle.

**Two sections, because they need different actions.** Measured 2026-09-06:
109 shipped-terminal tasks have no landing row, 3 have a branch at all, and 1
holds anything main lacks.

- **Unlanded work** — a branch exists and the probe reports commits main lacks.
  Actionable: land it, or reset the branch in place. This is the list that
  should be driven to zero.
- **No landing record** — no branch, or the branch holds nothing. Nothing to
  land; the record is missing. Not actionable by landing.

Rank the first section above the second and label both. Collapsing them into one
count would report ~109 outstanding items when 1 is actionable.

**Help text must contrast with its neighbour.** `task unlanded` and
`task unsettled` sit adjacent and look alike. Each opens by naming the
difference: `unsettled` asks whether a WORKTREE is modified or unlanded;
`unlanded` asks whether a TASK claims to be done while its work is not on main.

**Reuse `--project`, `--all`, `--llm`, `--json` and the row cap.** Match
`task landed`'s option set exactly — that is the point of the shared decorator.

## 3. `project status` claim

One attention claim, counting the **first** section only. The second section is
a standing historical count and would become permanent furniture.

```
 ⊘ 3 unlanded (Run: task unlanded)
```

Glyph and one-word label join the legend beside the existing claims. Suppress
the row entirely at zero.

Keep this coupling THIN. `project status` is heading for major revisions in
another session; specify the claim (count, glyph, drill-down verb) and leave the
rendering to that work rather than designing a row about to be replaced.

## 4. The authority banner

`task show`, `decision show` and their siblings lead with a banner when the
record is not straightforwardly authoritative. The status line is already on
screen and is demonstrably not enough — it is read as provenance, not caveat.

**Triggers.** Task: `obsolete`, `declined`, or carrying a `replaced_by` or
`duplicated_by` relation. Decision: `rejected`, `superseded`, or `proposed`.
Current volume: of 1391 tasks, 270 are obsolete/declined, 84 replaced, 3
duplicated; of 179 decisions, 124 accepted, 36 proposed, 18 rejected, 1
superseded. Roughly one record in four triggers, so three in four stay clean and
the banner keeps meaning something.

**Two kinds, named as such.** "Not ever" (obsolete, declined, rejected,
replaced, superseded) and "not yet" (proposed). The wording must distinguish
them; a proposed decision is not a retired one.

both the FIRST and LAST line, identical, not split, so whichever end survives a
`head -N` or `tail -N` is sufficient alone.

`agent_env.present()`, leaving the human-facing message unchanged. Carry that
here, so a human reading interactively sees the caveat once and an agent sees it
bracketed. Overturn it if the caveat is wanted twice for humans too.

gets a key, `--llm` gets the bracketed form since an agent reads it.

## 5. Guide

One paragraph next to §1's rendering, in the tasks section: a task status
answers "what did we decide about this work", never "where is the code". Point
at `task unlanded` for the latter, and at `task unsettled` for worktree state.

## 6. Data repair, same session

Fold this in rather than filing it (ED-1550 rule 2). Of the 109 shipped-terminal
tasks with no landing row, **20 have a commit on main attributed to them** and
should carry a landing record; 89 have no identifiable SHA and stay as they are.

Record each with `worktree land <id> --record-only --sha <sha>`.

**Verify every SHA before recording it.** The attribution came from grepping
commit messages, which over-credits: E-1048 was credited to a commit that merely
mentions it in the body while implementing E-1047. The bar is the one E-1150
met — its own description named the commit, and that commit is on main. A SHA
that cannot be verified to that standard is left unrecorded. Writing a
heuristic SHA into the table this report reads is the failure the report exists
to prevent.

This shrinks §2's second section. It does not affect the first.

## Verification

- `task show` on a terminal task with a landing row, without one and without a
  branch, and without one but with a branch holding commits — three distinct
  lines, no case rendering as blank.
- `task show` on a task whose branch is gone, and one whose probe errors —
  neither reads as clean.
- `task unlanded` sections ranked correctly, and `task unlanded --json` /
  `--llm` carrying the same split.
- `task unlanded --help` and `task unsettled --help` each name the other.
- Banner appears on an obsolete task, a replaced task, a proposed decision, and
  a rejected decision; is absent on an accepted decision and a confirmed task;
  survives both `| head -3` and `| tail -3`.
- After §6, the 20 tasks appear under `task landed` and have left `task
  unlanded`'s second section.

landed it — which this is. Filing a separate sweep task would be the
file-more-than-you-close behaviour that decision exists to stop.

Ordering, not scope, is what separates the two phases: the gate lands first, or
the sweep has nothing holding the line behind it.

Measured with the shipped predicate, against the main checkout:

- plans: 126 of 418 files carry a citation, 505 in total
- analyses: 23 of 131 files, 51 in total

Rewriting is per-file judgement, not a regex: each citation has to become the
function, command or symbol at that location, or the search that finds it. The
worst files carry twenty-odd each.

# E-698 — Fire-once background job runner

Decisions below were settled with Mike in session before implementation. Where a
decision reverses an earlier proposal, the reversal is noted.

## Scope

A fire-once runner: when invoked it executes any due jobs from a compile-time
job registry, then returns. Scheduling and repetition live in the **trigger**,
not the runner. Ships with **zero production jobs** — the registry is empty in
production and tests register fakes. E-1859 (evaluator) and E-1881 (auto-merge)
are the first real clients.

A general **fault-reporting facility** ships alongside it. It is deliberately
NOT owned by the runner: the runner is its first client, so the hook, land, and
reap can report through the same channel later (E-1884).

## Packages

| Package | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `internal/faults` | fault recording, incident dedupe, JSONL detail log, code catalog, read API |
| `internal/jobs` | `Job` interface, `Schedule`, registry, `RunDue` (the fire-once runner) |
| `internal/jobscmd` | `endless-go jobs list\|run\|retry` |
| `internal/errorscmd` | `endless-go errors show\|clear` |

New packages follow **ClearPath + doterr**, matching `internal/verify` (the
repo's newest Go package): named returns, `goto end`, sentinels in `errors.go`,
`doterr.NewErr` for wrapping. Older packages (`monitor`, `hookcmd`) are
idiomatic-Go and are not restyled here.

The Go package is named `faults` only because `errors` collides with the
stdlib package name. Every user-facing surface — the table, the CLI verb, the
docs — says **errors**.

## Schema (additive, `internal/schema/schema.sql`)

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS jobs (
    name             TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    next_due_at      TEXT NOT NULL,
    lease_owner      TEXT,
    lease_expires_at TEXT,
    last_run_at      TEXT,
    last_ok_at       TEXT,
    last_error       TEXT,
    run_count        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    fail_count       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S','now')),
    updated_at       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S','now'))
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS errors (
    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    code          TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'ERR-0001'
    severity      TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'warning' | 'error', from the catalog
    source        TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'job:<name>', later 'hook:PreToolUse', ...
    fingerprint   TEXT NOT NULL,
    summary       TEXT NOT NULL,   -- short descriptive text
    occurrences   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    first_seen_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    last_seen_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
    cleared_at    TEXT,
    cleared_by    TEXT
);

-- Incident model: at most ONE open row per fingerprint. A cleared row is
-- immutable history; a recurrence after clearing opens a NEW row so
-- "failed 40x, cleared, came back Tuesday" reads as two incidents.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS errors_open_uniq
    ON errors(source, code, fingerprint) WHERE cleared_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS errors_open_idx ON errors(cleared_at, severity);
```

No CHECK constraints (schema.sql house rule). Both tables are new, so the
standalone index statements are safe against pre-existing DBs.

## Fault detail — DB index + JSONL log

The DB row is the **index only**; it is bounded by distinct-fingerprint count,
not by failure count. Every occurrence's **full detail** appends one line to
`ConfigDir()/log/errors.jsonl`, carrying the incident id and occurrence number
so `errors show --detail` can pull it back.

Modeled directly on `internal/monitor/usermachinelog.go` (`user-machine.jsonl`):
append-only, best-effort, all write errors swallowed, `ConfigDir()`-routed so a
sandbox gets its own file. Explicitly **not** the shareable ledger.

**Faults emit no db-ledger events.** They are machine-local observation, not
shareable project history. (Verify: the ledger is driven by the events table,
so plain table writes produce nothing — assert this rather than assume it.)

## Error codes

`ERR-0001`, flat and unprefixed. No subsystem prefix: `JOB-`/`HOOK-` would squat
on namespace that project-scoped task IDs (`EDLS-NNNN`, per Mike) may want. The
`source` column already carries the subsystem.

Codes are `doterr` sentinels in the catalog, each with slug, severity, title and
a `docs/errors.md` anchor. A test gates: every catalog code has a docs section,
every docs section maps to a code, no duplicate numbers.

**Severity lives on the code**, not the call site, so two sites raising the same
condition cannot disagree about whether it is yellow or red.

## The runner

```go
type Schedule struct {
    Interval   time.Duration // normal cadence
    MaxBackoff time.Duration // 0 = no backoff: retry at Interval
    LeaseTTL   time.Duration // 0 = default max(2*Interval, 5m); also the ctx deadline
}

type Job interface {
    Name() string
    Schedule() Schedule
    Run(ctx context.Context) error
}

func Register(j Job)
func RunDue(ctx context.Context) Result
```

**Claim (compare-and-set).** One conditional UPDATE whose WHERE clause is the
mutual exclusion; `RowsAffected == 1` means we own it:

```sql
UPDATE jobs SET lease_owner = ?, lease_expires_at = datetime('now', ?)
 WHERE name = ? AND next_due_at <= datetime('now')
   AND (lease_owner IS NULL OR lease_expires_at <= datetime('now'))
```

Every timestamp is SQLite's `datetime('now')` — the "DB ticker". One shared
clock, so N concurrent monitors cannot disagree about whether a job is due.

**Lease.** Row-level and time-boxed, not an OS lock. A process that dies
mid-run needs no cleanup: the claim lapses and the next invocation re-claims.
Consequence to document on the interface: a merely *slow* job can be re-claimed
after expiry, so **jobs must be idempotent** and `LeaseTTL` must exceed expected
runtime generously.

**Backoff.** On success: `next_due = now + Interval`, `fail_count = 0`. On
failure: `fail_count++`, and when `MaxBackoff > 0`,
`next_due = now + min(Interval * 2^(fail_count-1), MaxBackoff)`; otherwise
`now + Interval`. A continuously failing job therefore decays to the cap — an
effective auto-disable, without ever going silently dark.

**Robustness — the monitor must never fall back to the CLI.**
- `recover()` per job, converted to a fault. An unrecovered panic in a job
  goroutine would kill the whole monitor process.
- Per-job `context` deadline = `LeaseTTL`. Honest caveat: Go cannot kill a
  goroutine that ignores `ctx`; a wedged job leaks one goroutine. Wedged is
  survivable, panicking is not.
- **The standard logger is swapped to a sink for the duration of the tick.**
  `log.Printf` writes to stderr; the monitor paints stdout with cursor-home
  escapes, so a log line lands on top of the drawn table — and since
  `monitorLoop` only repaints when the frame *changes*, the corruption persists
  indefinitely on an idle dashboard. 42 pre-existing call sites are converted
  separately (E-1884); this contains the seam E-698 creates.
- Every DB error inside the runner is recorded and swallowed, never propagated
  to the render path. The render path tolerates the tables being absent.
- The fault-recording path itself must not recurse when it fails.

## Trigger

`monitorLoop` fires `jobs.RunDue()` on a goroutine each 2s tick, behind a
single-in-flight `atomic.Bool` so a slow job never stacks up or blocks the
redraw. `endless-go jobs run` exists for E-1848's daemon, manual runs, and the
verify script.

## DB context — no bespoke rule

**Reversal.** An earlier proposal added a jobs-specific guard suppressing the
runner inside a self_dev worktree. Mike's constraint: don't proliferate
context rules users must learn. The established self_dev rule already exists
(E-1685, and every verify script): a worktree drives the candidate binary
against **its own sandbox**. `session status` / `session monitor` on their tmux
path were the exception — `PinMainDB()` at `session_status.go` overrides the
sandbox and reads the real DB.

So instead: **`sessionstatuscmd` skips `PinMainDB` when cwd is a self_dev
worktree**, and the runner gets **no special rule** — it uses the resolved DB
context like every other command. In a worktree that resolves to the sandbox,
which the worktree binary owns, so E-1818 schema-passivity does not apply and
the new tables are created normally.

Known cost, accepted: in a worktree the dashboard will not pane-resolve a focal
task, because the sandbox-seeded session row has no `process` and only the hook
(which pins main) ever sets one. It shows the "no session" hint instead. Mike
does not run the dashboard from worktrees; this is strictly better than silently
reading the real DB. The underlying machine-vs-project split is **E-1883**.

## User-facing surface

```
endless errors show [--all] [--detail]   # open incidents; --all includes cleared
endless errors clear [<id>...|--all]     # marks cleared, never deletes
endless jobs list                        # registry + schedule + last run + fails
endless jobs run                         # fire once, now
endless jobs retry <name>                # "I fixed it": next_due = now, fail_count = 0
```

`errors clear` and `jobs retry` are deliberately separate verbs: clearing means
"I have seen this", retrying means "I have fixed this". Fusing them would let an
acknowledgement silently re-arm a job that is still broken.

Python exposes these as thin delegating wrappers threading the `--db` context,
mirroring `session_status_resolve` in `src/endless/session_cmd.py`.

## The badge

`renderSnapshot` appends a trailing line when open incidents exist — rendered by
**both** `session status` and `session monitor`, since they share the renderer
and the one-shot is the more frequently seen surface. Max severity wins
(error > warning), with per-severity counts, the latest short text, and the
`endless errors show` affordance. Respects the existing `color` flag; no ANSI
when not a TTY. `eraseEachLineToEOL` handles the extra line unchanged.

## Verification

`tests/tasks/e-698-verify.sh`, fail-fast, folding this task's own tests in:

1. Go unit tests for `internal/jobs` and `internal/faults` (fail fast).
2. CAS claim under real concurrency: N processes race one due job, exactly one
   wins.
3. Lease expiry re-claim; a killed owner's job is re-claimable.
4. Backoff math, and reset on success.
5. Panic in a job is recovered, recorded as a fault, and does not kill the run.
6. Incident dedupe: repeats bump `occurrences`; clear-then-recur opens a NEW row.
7. JSONL detail written and readable back; no db-ledger event emitted.
8. Catalog/docs sync gate.
9. End-to-end through the CLI: `jobs list`/`run`/`retry`, `errors show`/`clear`.
10. Badge renders in both `session status` and `session monitor` frames.
11. `session-status` no longer pins main inside a self_dev worktree.

## Deltas from the plan as implemented

- **Guide coverage written, not deferred.** `jobs` and `errors` are new
  user-facing verbs, so `just guide-check` (a pre-land gate) failed with "no map
  file at all". Rather than declare a `gap:` — the established escape hatch, used
  by seven existing commands — both got real sections in `docs/guide/reference.md`
  plus map files, and the generated cross-reference was regenerated.
- **The Python wrapper reuses `event_bridge._resolve_endless_go`.** A first pass
  used `shutil.which`, which finds the GLOBAL binary — the new subcommands exist
  only in the candidate build, so every `endless jobs …` call failed with
  "unknown subcommand" until it landed. The existing resolver already prefers
  `<worktree>/bin/endless-go` under `--db sandbox` (E-1510) for the same class of
  reason.
- **A planned test was wrong and was replaced.** "Faults emit no db-ledger
  events" was drafted as a query against an `events` TABLE. There is no such
  table — the ledger is an append-only directory of segment files
  (`internal/events/writer.go`). The invariant is now asserted two ways that are
  actually true: recording a fault creates nothing but `errors.jsonl`, and
  `internal/faults` has no build dependency on `internal/events`.
- **Reap was NOT migrated**, as decided. It remains fired opportunistically from
  five hook sites plus land/claim. Its migration is a candidate for the runner
  once a real job exists to model it on.

## Filed during this task

- **E-1883** (brainstorm) — db-ledger is project-scoped but `endless.db` is
  machine-global, so a rebuild loses other projects. Second, independent driver
  found here: session-status's main-pin vs sandbox-routed tasks is the same
  machine-vs-project split.
- **E-1884** — convert the 42 `log.Printf` call sites to the fault system.

# E-894 — Move task-display DB reads from Python to Go

> Refreshed 2026-05-26 against current `main` (HEAD survey). Supersedes the
> 2026-05-02 plan, whose "focus pilot" template and `migrate.go` framework
> assumptions are stale (see Reconciliation below).

## Goal

Move every task-display DB **read** out of Python and into Go, so Python has
zero SQLite knowledge for task operations. Python keeps rendering (Rich tables,
markdown, tree, `--json`, `--llm`); only the data-fetch step moves. Decoupling
scope: **full** (Phases 1-3) per decision with Mike 2026-05-26 — also retire
Python's schema bootstrap so Go owns DB creation.

## Reconciliation with current main (what changed since 2026-05-02)

- **No "focus pilot" to mirror.** The old plan said it would copy an established
  `query_bridge.py` + `internal/events/query.go` + `endless-event get-focus`
  read pattern. That code was never landed (stranded uncommitted in an orphaned
  `e-1031` worktree) and is abandoned. We build the read pattern **fresh**,
  mirroring the **write** bridge (`event_bridge.py`) instead. E-1053, which
  formalized that pilot, is obsoleted.
- **Schema framework is gone.** E-1459 deleted the E-863 `migrate.go` versioned
  framework and replaced it with `internal/schema/schema.sql` (authoritative,
  applied by Go on every `monitor.DB()` open) + one-shot `internal/schema/changes/*`.
  The forward schema is **already Go-owned**. So the old "port V5/V6 migrations
  into Go" work is **moot**; Phase 3 is now pure deletion of Python's bootstrap,
  not migration porting. (No migration logic is written — none is needed.)
- **Read-site drift:** all read functions still exist; `_project_root_for_task`
  is now `_main_root_for_task` (`task_cmd.py`); the `session_cmd.py`
  task read is now `:1434`. `suggestions_cmd.py` has **no** task reads — it drops
  off the worklist.
- **`endless-event` uses raw stdlib** `switch os.Args[1]` + per-subcommand
  `flag.NewFlagSet` (no go-cliutil); first call is `monitor.ConsumeDBContextFlag()`.
  New read subcommands follow that same internal-binary style.

## The pattern (mirror the write bridge)

Writes today: `event_bridge.py` → `shutil.which("endless-event")` +
`config.require_db_context()` + `*config.go_db_context_args()` (the E-1429
`--config-dir` threading) → `subprocess.run(capture_output, text)` →
`json.loads(stdout)`. Reads mirror this exactly via a new `query_bridge.py`.

**CRITICAL:** the read bridge MUST inject `*config.go_db_context_args()` right
after the binary name, exactly as `event_bridge.py` does, or reads trip
the E-1429 worktree DB-context gate (`monitor.guardWorktreeDBContext`).

**JSON I/O convention:**
- Single-row query → one JSON object on stdout, or literal `null` if not found.
- List query → JSON array, or `[]` if empty.
- Error → stderr prefixed `endless-event: error:`, exit 1 (exit 2 for missing
  required flags).
- Output shapes must carry **every field** Python's default / `--json` / `--llm`
  formatters consume today (capture per-command during Phase 1).

**Phase 1 subcommand surface:**

| Subcommand | Replaces (Python) | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `get-task --id N` | `detail_item` core query | object/null |
| `list-tasks [filters]` | `show_plan` | array |
| `next-tasks [filters --limit N]` | `next_tasks` | array |
| `search-tasks --query S [...]` | `search_tasks` | array |
| `task-children --id N` | `detail_item --children` | array |
| `task-relations --id N [--rel-type T]` | `get_all_relations` / `_related_task_ids` / `show_relations` | array |
| `active-tasks` | `active_tasks` | array |
| `recent-tasks [--limit N]` | `recent_tasks` | array |
| `list-decisions [filters]` | `list_decisions` | array |
| `task-by-source-file --path P` | `_main_root_for_task` SQL | object/null |

Filters mirror the Click flags: `--phase --status --tier --parent --related-to
--rel-type --all --sort --limit`.

## DRY sources (lift, don't rewrite)

- `internal/web/queries.go`: `GetProjectTasks` (≈ `show_plan`: tree + child_count
  + blocked_by GROUP_CONCAT), `GetCurrentWork` (≈ `active_tasks`),
  `GetProjectDependencies` (≈ `get_all_relations`), plus group/detail helpers.
  These bind to web `data.*` view structs — extract the SQL/scan into a shared
  read helper, then have web reuse it.
- `internal/monitor/task.go`: `GetActiveTasks`, `TaskText`, `GetProjectName`.
- Go DB handle: `monitor.DB()` (`internal/monitor/db.go`); path honors the
  E-1429 dbContextDir then XDG.

## Phases (each is a child task; gate on prior phase landing; own worktree each)

1. **Add Go read subcommands to `endless-event`** (child task). Go read helpers +
   the 10 subcommands above; lift overlapping SQL from `web/queries.go`; per-helper
   tests. No Python change.
2. **Add `query_bridge.py` + cut every task read over** (child, blocked by P1).
   New bridge mirroring `event_bridge.py` (incl. `--config-dir`); replace each
   `db.query` task read; delete the dead Python SQL bodies; golden-output parity.
3. **Remove Python's schema bootstrap** (child, blocked by P2). Delete
   `_init_schema`/`_migrate*` from `db.py`; Go owns DB creation; subsumes the
   E-1116 empty-DB crash. **Scope note:** db.py's `query()` stays — Python still
   reads non-task tables (sessions/projects/suggestions); those are out of scope.
   "Python has zero SQLite knowledge" applies to **tasks**, not all tables.

## Out of scope

- Web/TUI reads (already Go). P1 lifts shared SQL so web reuses it; no UI cutover.
- Non-task table reads (sessions/projects/suggestions) — separate future tasks.
- Goal/focus subsystem — entirely unbuilt on main; E-894 has zero dependency.
- Any migration logic (none needed; forward schema already in `schema.sql`).

## Decision log

- 2026-05-26 (Mike): **full decouple, Phases 1-3** — the schema phase is cheap
  now that E-1459 moved forward schema to Go; do it rather than leave Python a
  SQLite foothold.
- 2026-05-26 (Mike): **start fresh, no salvage** of the stranded `e-1031` pilot.
- 2026-05-26: reconcile-then-spawn; this session does DB-only planning (no claim,
  no worktree); implementation spawned per-phase.

## Closeout (E-894 has no code of its own)

E-894 is the umbrella; all implementation lives in the phase children. Endless
has **no automatic parent rollup** — confirming the children does NOT flip the
parent. So once **E-1481, E-1482, and E-1484 are all confirmed**, set
**E-894 → verify** (`endless task update E-894 --status verify`); Mike confirms
E-894. The terminal phase (E-1484) carries the same reminder so the spawned
session that finishes the chain does the flip.

fields.description: Refactor monitor.IsCheckEnabled in internal/monitor/checks.go to call internal/config.Load(projectPath) and read cfg.Checks[name] with fallback to per-check defaults. Delete the existing bespoke reader (entire file becomes unnecessary; the default helper moves to internal/config/normalize.go per the parent plan). Callsite is cmd/endless-hook/claude.go. With this in place, setting checks.drift_detection in either ~/.config/endless/config.json (global) OR <proj>/.endless/config.json (per-project) must work, with project key overriding global key (per-key merge confirmed by Mike).

Currently 'endless task update' prints '• Updated E-###: status' listing only field names. Should print 'status=ready' (or similar) showing the new value for every changed field. Source: src/endless/task_cmd.py. The fields dict already holds the values; iterate fields.items() and render key=value pairs. Truncate long blobs (text, prompt) to a short preview or just show '<set>' / '<cleared>'. Handle None as 'cleared' or '∅' for parent_id/tier clears.

Two verbs hit during E-968 work: 'verify' (legitimate action verb for verification tasks) and 'reconcile' (legitimate action verb for sync/cleanup work). Both blocked by validate_title in src/endless/task_cmd.py. Add them to _TITLE_VERBS so future tasks with these verbs aren't blocked. Will be obsoleted by E-970 (phrases table) but worth fixing now to stop wasting verbs as friction.

While building E-989 we articulated the criteria for non-fatal-on-error: opportunistic by design, self-healing on a later event, or high expected error rate. Audit snapshotPlanFile (cmd/endless-hook/claude.go), which currently swallows errors with log.Printf and returns nil, against those criteria. If it qualifies, document the rationale in a comment; otherwise convert to fatal, matching InitSession / SetProcess / WriteCompanion. Out of scope: a sweep of every other log.Printf-on-err site in the hook.
