# Render analysis in `endless task show` + `--all-fields` flag

## Problem
`tasks.analysis` is settable via `endless task add/update --analysis` (cli.py) but
`endless task show` (`detail_item`, task_cmd.py) never renders it — analysis content
is write-only from the CLI (visible only via the web UI / raw SQL). E-999 (in_progress) already
names this gap; this task delivers just the read surface. The text→plan rename (E-1000) is out
of scope.

## Implementation
1. `task show` CLI (cli.py): add a `--analysis`/`show_analysis` flag (parallel to
   `--text`/`--outcome`), passed into `detail_item`. Add `--all-fields` that turns on
   description + analysis + text + outcome + children in one switch, so handoffs can request
   complete task content without enumerating each flag.
2. `detail_item` (task_cmd.py ~3445): render a cyan `— Analysis —` section. Order:
   Description → Analysis → Text → Outcome (analysis is pre-plan design content, so it precedes
   the plan). Include analysis in the `--llm` and `--json` output paths too.
3. Fix the validator help strings (task_cmd.py, 375) that wrongly steer long-form analysis
   to `--text`; they predate/contradict E-999's analysis-vs-plan separation.

## Tests
- New `tests/test_analysis_show.py` (or extend an existing show test): set `--analysis` on a
  task; assert `task show --analysis` emits `— Analysis —` with the content; assert
  `--all-fields` emits every content section; assert default `task show` still omits analysis.

## Verify
- `endless task update <t> --analysis "X"; endless task show <t> --analysis` shows `— Analysis —`
  with `X`; `endless task show <t> --all-fields` shows every content section; `just test` green.

## Out of scope
- text→plan rename (E-1000); analysis content-rule enforcement (E-1073 / E-1075).

# E-1601 — Gate large fields in `task show` behind display flags

## Goal

Make `endless task show <id>` a true **snapshot** by default: it never dumps a
large field's full content unless explicitly asked, and when a large field is
hidden it prints a one-line placeholder advertising the flag that reveals it
(e.g. `Outcome: 1275 chars (--outcome to display)` — the number is computed via
`len()`; 1275 is illustrative).

Today the **outcome** field auto-displays in full whenever a task's status is
`declined` or `completed` (`task_cmd.py`), regardless of flags. For a
research/epic task whose deliverable *is* the outcome (e.g. E-1600, ~38KB), this
floods the snapshot and — via `--llm` — burns a large token budget on an
inspection the guide tells agents to run routinely.

## Decisions (resolved with Mike, 2026-06-20)

1. **Suppress uniformly.** Drop the status-based auto-display entirely. Outcome
   shows in full only with `--outcome` (or `--all-fields`). This includes
   `declined`: the decline reason becomes a placeholder too. One predictable
   rule; the reason is one keystroke away.
2. **All three large fields get the treatment.** `text`, `analysis`, and
   `outcome` each render a char-count placeholder when hidden. `description`
   is unchanged (shown by default, `--no-description` hides it with no
   placeholder).
3. **Consistent across all three output modes** — human, `--llm`, `--json`.

No new flags are needed: `--outcome`/`--text`/`--analysis`/`--all-fields`
already exist and already drive `show_outcome`/`show_text`/`show_analysis`.

## Implementation

All changes are in `src/endless/task_cmd.py::detail_item` plus one help-string
edit in `src/endless/cli.py`. No schema, no Go, no migration.

### 1. Human-readable path (`task_cmd.py`)

Replace the four hand-rolled large-text blocks with calls to a small helper so
the full-vs-placeholder logic lives in one place:

```python
def _echo_large_field(title: str, content: str | None, show: bool, flag: str):
    """Render a large text field for `task show`. Full content (titled
    section) when `show`; otherwise a one-line char-count placeholder naming
    the flag that reveals it. No output when the field is empty."""
    if not content:
        return
    click.echo()
    if show:
        click.echo(click.style(f"— {title} —", fg="cyan"))
        click.echo(content)
    else:
        click.echo(
            click.style(f"{title}:", fg="cyan")
            + " "
            + click.style(f"{len(content)} chars", fg="white", bold=True)
            + click.style(f" ({flag} to display)", dim=True)
        )
```

Call order is unchanged (Analysis, then Text, then Outcome — preserving the
E-999 / E-1577 ordering):

```python
# Description keeps its existing default-on behaviour (no placeholder).
if show_description and item["description"] and item["description"] != item["title"]:
    click.echo()
    click.echo(click.style("— Description —", fg="cyan"))
    click.echo(item["description"])

_echo_large_field("Analysis", item["analysis"], show_analysis, "--analysis")
_echo_large_field("Text",     item["text"],     show_text,     "--text")
_echo_large_field("Outcome",  item["outcome"],  show_outcome,  "--outcome")
```

The status check (`item["status"] in ("declined", "completed")`) is **removed**.

### 2. `--llm` path (`task_cmd.py`)

- **Remove** the unconditional top-of-block dump:
  `if item["outcome"]: click.echo(f"outcome={item['outcome']}")` (3386-3387).
- After the `landed=` line, emit a compact char marker for each large field
  that is present but hidden:

  ```python
  for name, content, show in (
      ("analysis", item["analysis"], show_analysis),
      ("text",     item["text"],     show_text),
      ("outcome",  item["outcome"],  show_outcome),
  ):
      if content and not show:
          click.echo(f"{name}_chars={len(content)}")
  ```

- Keep the existing `## Description/Analysis/Text` full sections (gated by their
  show flags) and **add** a matching `## Outcome` section:

  ```python
  if show_outcome and item["outcome"]:
      click.echo(f"\n## Outcome\n{item['outcome']}")
  ```

Net effect: `task show --llm` on E-1600 emits `outcome_chars=NNNNN` instead of
the full deliverable; `task show --llm --outcome` emits the full `## Outcome`.

### 3. `--json` path (`task_cmd.py`)

Gate `outcome` like `text`/`analysis` already are, and add always-present
char counts so the JSON shape stays stable and machine-readable:

```python
"outcome": item["outcome"] if show_outcome else None,
"outcome_chars": len(item["outcome"]) if item["outcome"] else None,
"text_chars": len(item["text"]) if item["text"] else None,
"analysis_chars": len(item["analysis"]) if item["analysis"] else None,
```

(`text` / `analysis` content keys keep their existing show-flag gating.)

### 4. Help text (`cli.py`)

Change the `--outcome` help from
`"Show outcome field (always shown for declined tasks)"`
to
`"Show the full outcome field (hidden by default; a char-count placeholder shows otherwise)"`.

## Existing tests to UPDATE (they encode the old behavior)

In `tests/test_outcome.py`:

- `test_task_show_declined_always_shows_outcome` (157) — rename to
  `test_task_show_declined_hides_outcome_by_default` and assert the placeholder:
  output contains `Outcome:` and `(--outcome to display)`, and does **not**
  contain `— Outcome —` nor the full reason text. Add a sibling that passes
  `--outcome` and asserts the full `— Outcome —` section + reason text appear.
- `test_task_show_llm_includes_outcome` (186) — without a flag, assert
  `outcome_chars=` appears and `outcome=llm-mode reason` does **not**; add a
  `--outcome` case asserting `## Outcome` + the reason.
- `test_task_show_json_includes_outcome` (195) — without a flag, assert
  `parsed["outcome"] is None` and `parsed["outcome_chars"] == len(reason)`; add
  a `--outcome` case asserting `parsed["outcome"] == reason`.
- `test_task_show_outcome_flag_renders_outcome` (144) and
  `test_task_show_outcome_section_renders_after_text` (169) — these pass
  `--outcome`/`--text --outcome` and should still pass unchanged; re-run to
  confirm.

## New tests to ADD (`tests/test_outcome.py`)

- Placeholder char count is accurate: set a known-length outcome, no flag,
  assert `Outcome: <len> chars (--outcome to display)` in output.
- `--all-fields` reveals the full outcome section (no placeholder).
- `completed` task without `--outcome` shows the placeholder (regression guard
  for the E-1600 scenario that motivated this).
- `text` and `analysis` placeholders render with correct flag names when those
  fields are set and their flags are absent.

## Verify script — `tests/tasks/e-1601-verify.sh` (deliverable)

Write an ad-hoc per-task verify script following the **same shape** as the
existing `tests/tasks/e-1599-verify.sh` — which already exercises the adjacent
`task show` field-rendering surface, so reuse its scaffolding verbatim:

- `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, `set -u`, TTY-aware color helpers.
- `section` / `report_pass` / `report_fail` / `summary` reporters; exit `0`
  all-passed, `1` any failure, `2` environment error (not a git worktree / no
  `uv`).
- `endless() { uv run endless "$@" --db sandbox; }` so every behavioral check
  runs against the worktree sandbox DB, never the real ledger.
- `add_task_get_id` helper; `assert_contains` / `assert_not_contains` /
  `assert_ordering` assertions. Add a tiny `repeat_a N` helper to build a
  known-length body so char-count assertions are exact.

This is an **ad-hoc per-task script**, not a deliverable of the in-flight
verification-suite epic (E-1596) — it mirrors `e-1599-verify.sh`'s reference
shape, exactly as that script frames itself.

### Checks the script must cover

1. **Default snapshot hides outcome + shows placeholder.** Task with a
   known-length outcome → `task show` (no flags) `contains` `Outcome:`,
   the exact `N chars` count, and `(--outcome to display)`; `not_contains`
   `— Outcome —` nor the outcome body.
2. **`--outcome` reveals the full section.** `contains` `— Outcome —` + body;
   `not_contains` `(--outcome to display)`.
3. **Uniform suppression for declined.** Declined task → default `task show`
   shows the placeholder, `not_contains` `— Outcome —` nor the reason; with
   `--outcome` the reason returns. (Guards the dropped status-based auto-display.)
4. **`text` / `analysis` placeholders.** Set both → default show `contains`
   `Text: <len> chars (--text to display)` and
   `Analysis: <len> chars (--analysis to display)`, bodies absent.
5. **Char-count accuracy.** Outcome of exactly L chars (via `repeat_a L`) →
   output `contains` `Outcome: L chars`.
6. **`--all-fields` reveals everything.** `contains` `— Outcome —`, `— Text —`,
   `— Analysis —`; `not_contains` any `(--… to display)` placeholder.
7. **`--llm` gating.** Default `--llm` `contains` `outcome_chars=L` and
   `not_contains` the full outcome body / `outcome=`; `--llm --outcome`
   `contains` `## Outcome` + body.
8. **`--json` gating.** Default `--json` `contains` `"outcome": null` and
   `"outcome_chars": L`; `--json --outcome` `contains` `"outcome": "<body>"`.
9. **Pytest regression suite passes.** Final `section` runs `just test` (capture
   output) and `report_pass`/`report_fail` on its exit code, so a single
   invocation of the script is the whole gate — the updated/added
   `test_outcome.py` cases plus the black-box checks above, all in one
   ALL PASSED / failure summary.

## Verification

`./tests/tasks/e-1601-verify.sh` is the single gate. Open `esu` into the
worktree and run it; `ALL PASSED` (exit 0) means every check above — including
the pytest suite via check 9 — is green. Any failure prints the expected/got
detail per check for diagnosis.

## Out of scope

- `description` placeholder behavior (stays default-on).
- Any Go `task show` path (the live command is the Python `detail_item`).
- Length-based auto-truncation / "show first N lines" — explicit flag gating is
  the agreed model.

# Plan — E-1605: testscript/txtar + pytest forms + first dogfood suites

## Context

The E-1596 epic builds Endless's per-task verification-suite system. Its foundation
trio has landed: E-1602 (manifest schema + discovery), E-1603 (the Tier-0
`endless-go verify` runner), E-1604 (CTRF-subset writer + `gotest-json`/`pytest-json`/`tap`
normalizers + the first-class `gotest`/`pytest` shortcut registry). Two runner *forms*
the system still lacks in practice: an end-to-end **txtar/testscript** form for Go CLIs,
and a working **pytest** form. This task adds both and proves the whole stack with the
first two real `.endless/tasks/<id>/verify.toml` suites (converting the interim
`tests/tasks/e-16{03,58}-verify.sh` bash scripts into product suites). Do **not** retrofit
any of the other interim `tests/tasks/*-verify.sh` scripts in this task — only the two named
exemplars; the broader interim-script cleanup is a separate concern.

A design fork surfaced during planning and was resolved with Mike: the first-class
`pytest` shortcut (our own code, `internal/verify/check.go`) emits a bare `pytest …`
command, but this project is uv-managed and `pytest` isn't on PATH. Decision: **make it
just work** by resolving the Python test launcher through an **adapter** rather than
layering tool-specific conditionals into the generic runner. The adapter prefers
`.venv/bin/pytest` (a plain executable — no uv, no network, survives the runner's
temp-HOME isolation), then `uv run pytest`, then bare `pytest`. Other Python tools
(poetry/pdm) plug in as future adapters; the raw-command path covers them meanwhile.
**Status: complete.** The launcher-resolution design went through the brainstorm **E-1789**
(ED-1535/1536/1537) and its implementation **E-1791**, which landed the `RunnerDriver`
interface + the `pytest/uv` driver (launcher precedence `.venv/bin/pytest` → `uv run
--no-sync pytest` → bare `pytest`). E-1605 rebased onto that and finished the pytest slice:
the E-1603 suite's `pytest/uv` check + `tests/test_verify_cmd.py`. §2 below is retained as
the original design record; the shipped mechanism is E-1791's driver, not an in-task adapter.

## Key facts established

- Runner executes each `[[check]]` via `sh -c` with cwd = the **project root discovered
  from cwd** (`findProjectRoot` walks up to the first `.endless/`) — the **worktree** in a
  self-dev session, not main; isolation replaces only `HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (PATH
  preserved), no temp working dir: `internal/verifycmd/env.go`.
- First-class registry + command emission: `internal/verify/check.go`
  (`firstClassRunners`, `translateGotest`/`captureGotest`, `translatePytest`/`capturePytest`,
  `Check.ResolvedCommand()`, `Check.CaptureCommand(reportPath)`).
- Only two emission call sites: `internal/verify/runscript.go` (bare-clone) and
  `internal/verifycmd/env.go` (capture).
- Formats supported: `gotest-json`, `pytest-json`, `tap` (`internal/verify/normalize.go`).
  A txtar suite needs **no new format** — testscript runs under `go test`, captured as `gotest`.
- SUT for the E-1758 exemplar: `monitor.WorktreeAnomaliesAt(projectRoot, worktreePath)`
  (`internal/monitor/worktree_anomalies.go`), reached via the CLI

Rationale: `maybe` = uncommitted; parent-child = scope binding. A parent with maybe-phase children has *phantom scope* — it appears done while uncommitted commitments linger inside, and it breaks epic auto-derivation (E-1541), which can't safely treat maybe children as part of the parent's outcome. The `relates_to` link type preserves conceptual adjacency without violating the invariant. This task enforces that invariant as a **hard gate** (no `--force` escape) on every write path that can produce the forbidden state. ## The single invariant All described operations reduce to one rule, evaluated against the **resulting** row state: > Reject when effective `phase == "maybe"` AND effective `parent_id` is not NULL. # E-1617: Remove verb-completability gate on epic-type tasks

## Context

The verb-completability gate (`_require_completable_verb_for_completed` in
`src/endless/task_cmd.py`, from E-1240/ED-1502) reserves the `completed` status
for findings-as-deliverable work by requiring the task title's lead verb to be
marked `completable: true` in `verbs.json` (audit, research, review, …). It keeps
implementation tasks on the `verify → confirmed/assumed` track.

Epics (E-1577 / ED-1503) are a different shape: a type=epic task's deliverable
**is** its outcome text (a coordination summary of what shipped in its children),
and the type gate already forces epics to terminate via `completed` (research/epic
reject `assumed`/`confirmed`). But an epic's title typically leads with an
implementation verb like "implement", which the verb gate rejects for `completed`.
The two gates contradict — a concrete deadlock was hit on **E-1564** (type=epic,
lead verb "implement"): the type gate demands `completed`, the verb gate forbids it.

**ED-1511** resolves this: when `tasks.type = 'epic'`, skip the verb gate — the
type gate alone is correct enforcement. Research is unaffected (its natural lead
verbs — research/audit/investigate — are already `completable`), so the decision
is scoped to epic only.

## Change

Make `_require_completable_verb_for_completed` type-aware and skip it for epics,
mirroring the existing `_require_terminal_allowed_for_type` pattern that already
takes a task type.

### 1. `_require_completable_verb_for_completed` — add `task_type` param (≈line 1918)

Add a third parameter and an early return for epics:

```python
def _require_completable_verb_for_completed(
    status: str | None,
    title: str | None,
    task_type: str | None = None,
):
    """E-1240: `completed` is gated to tasks whose title's lead verb is
    marked `completable: true` in verbs.json. … ED-1511: epics are exempt —
    an epic's deliverable IS its outcome text, and the type gate already
    requires `completed`, so the verb gate would only deadlock them."""
    if status != "completed":
        return
    if task_type == "epic":
        return
    ...
```

### 2. `mark_completed_item` call site (≈lines 2133–2144)

The pre-check query selects only `id, title, status` — add the type slug so the
gate can see it, then pass it through:

```python
row = db.query(
    "SELECT id, COALESCE(title, description) as title, status, "
    "       COALESCE((SELECT slug FROM task_types WHERE id = tasks.type_id), '') AS type "
    "FROM tasks WHERE id = ?",
    (item_id,),
)
...
_require_completable_verb_for_completed("completed", row[0]["title"], row[0]["type"])
```

(The `COALESCE((SELECT slug …), '')` subquery is the exact pattern already used in
`update_plan`'s query at line 3100.)

### 3. `update_plan` call site (≈lines 3135–3141)

`effective_type` is already computed here for `_require_terminal_allowed_for_type`,
but **after** the verb-gate call. Move that one line up so both gates share it:

```python
effective_title = title if title is not None else row[0]["title"]
effective_type = task_type if task_type is not None else row[0]["type"]
_require_completable_verb_for_completed(status, effective_title, effective_type)
# E-1577: research/epic tasks reject 'assumed'/'confirmed' terminals.
_require_terminal_allowed_for_type(status, effective_type)
```

## Tests — `tests/test_completed_status.py`

- Extend the `_add_task` helper with a `type_id: int = 1` parameter (epic = 4 per
  `internal/schema/schema.sql`) so tests can create epics.
- Add cases (the deadlock fix):
  - `mark_completed_item` on an epic with a non-completable verb ("Implement X")
    + outcome → succeeds, status becomes `completed`.
  - `update_plan(status="completed", outcome=…)` on an epic with "Implement X"
    → succeeds.
- Add a regression guard: a **non-epic** (`type=task`) with "Implement X" still
  raises (verb gate intact for implementation tasks) — the existing
  `test_completed_rejects_implementation_verb` already covers this; add one
  asserting the epic/non-epic distinction explicitly so the exemption can't
  silently widen.

## Verify script — `tests/tasks/e-1617-verify.sh`

Per the convention prototyped under E-1596 (`tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh`, et al.),
add an executable ad-hoc verification script that exercises the fix **end-to-end
through the CLI** against the worktree's sandbox DB. Reuse that file's harness shape
verbatim — same `endless() { uv run endless "$@" --db sandbox; }` wrapper, the
`add_task_get_id`, `assert_succeeds`, `assert_refused`, `assert_contains` helpers,
the `section`/`report_pass`/`report_fail`/`summary` reporting, `set -u`, color-when-tty,
`cd` to `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, exit 0 on ALL PASSED / 1 on any failure.

Checks (the deadlock fix + regression guards that the exemption didn't widen):

- **Fix — epic via `task complete`:** create `--type epic` titled "Implement the foo
  subsystem", then `task complete <id> --outcome "shipped via children"` → **succeeds**
  (pre-fix: "requires a completable lead verb").
- **Fix — epic via `task update`:** epic "Implement bar", then
  `task update <id> --status completed --outcome "…"` → **succeeds**.
- **Regression — plain task still gated:** `--type task` titled "Implement baz",
  `task complete <id> --outcome "done"` → **refused**, output contains `completable`.
- **Regression — completable verb on plain task still works:** `--type task` titled
  "Audit qux", `task complete --outcome` → **succeeds** (verb gate intact, not disabled).
- **Other epic gates intact (the exemption is narrow):**
  - epic completed still requires outcome: `task complete <epic>` (no `--outcome`)
    → **refused**, output contains `outcome is required`.
  - epic still rejects `assumed`/`confirmed` (type gate, E-1577):
    `task update <epic> --status confirmed` → **refused**.

The script is committed with the change. It is reference-shape only (E-1596 will
formalize the framework); it must require no external tools beyond `uv` + the sandbox.

## Files

- `src/endless/task_cmd.py` — gate function + two call sites.
- `tests/test_completed_status.py` — helper + new cases.
- `tests/tasks/e-1617-verify.sh` — new executable end-to-end verify script (chmod +x).

No schema change, no verbs.json change.

## Verification

```sh
esu e-1617          # cd worktree + export ENDLESS_SESSION_ID
just build          # stale Go bins reject nothing here, but keep toolchain coherent
just test           # full Python suite; new + existing cases green
```

Targeted run: `just test -- tests/test_completed_status.py` (or pytest filter on
the new epic cases).

End-to-end (the committed verify script, sandbox-routed, run from inside the worktree):

```sh
./tests/tasks/e-1617-verify.sh
# → prints pass/fail per check, then "ALL PASSED" (exit 0)
```

This covers the epic-completes path, the plain-task regression guards, and the
still-intact outcome/terminal gates without touching the real DB.

## Closeout

`endless task update E-1617 --status verify --db main`, hand Mike the how-to-test,
and the return line. Do not land/drop without asking.

# E-1620: Render hierarchical task context in bg agent labels for Agent View

## Context

When `endless task spawn --bg` dispatches a background Claude agent, it labels it
two ways: the `--name` arg to `claude --bg` and the opening identity line of the
rendered handoff (which Claude's own title-inference may pick up). Both currently
encode only the bare task id (`E-<id>`), with no parent/epic context. In the
global Agent View, a child of an epic is therefore indistinguishable from a
standalone task, and there is no native epic-scoped filtering to compensate.

This change makes every bg-agent label self-identify by hierarchy:

- root task (no parent — standalone or epic) → `E-<id>: <title>`
- any task with a parent (child of an epic OR of any other task) → `E-<parent>/E-<id>: <title>`

The single distinguishing rule is **parent_id present → prefix with
`E-<parent>/`**, regardless of the parent's type. The spec's "standalone vs epic
vs child of an epic" framing collapses to this: roots (standalone and epic) share
one shape; anything with a parent gets the parent-prefixed shape. Decisions
confirmed with Mike:
the text after the prefix is the task **title** (not `description`), and both id
segments carry the `E-` prefix (`E-1564/E-1620`).

## Reproduction (current behavior)

E-1620 is a child of epic E-1564. Today:
- `--name` is built as `f"E-{item_id}"` → `E-1620` (`src/endless/task_cmd.py`).
- Handoff line 3 renders `- E-1620: <title>.` (`internal/templatecmd/templates/handoff/*.md.tmpl:3`).

Neither shows the parent epic. After the change the same dispatch yields
`E-1564/E-1620: <title>`.

## Implementation

### 1. New helper — `src/endless/task_cmd.py`
Add a pure function near `task_id_display` (line 385):
```python
def _hierarchical_label_prefix(item_id: int, parent_id: int | None) -> str:
    """E-<parent>/E-<id> when the task has a parent, else E-<id> (E-1620)."""
    if parent_id:
        return f"{task_id_display(parent_id)}/{task_id_display(item_id)}"
    return task_id_display(item_id)
```

### 2. Thread `parent_id` into the spawn path — `src/endless/task_cmd.py`
- The `spawn_plan` task query (line ~3811) already selects the task row in
  Python; add `p.parent_id` to its SELECT list (one extra column on an existing
  read — no new `db.query` site, consistent with the function's current pattern).
- Pass `item["parent_id"]` to `_spawn_bg_dispatch` (new param).

### 3. `_spawn_bg_dispatch` — `src/endless/task_cmd.py` (~4137)
- Accept `parent_id: int | None`.
- Compute `prefix = _hierarchical_label_prefix(item_id, parent_id)` once.
- `--name`: change `f"E-{item_id}"` → `f"{prefix}: {title}"` (full label, matching
  the spec shape; line 4172).
- Pass `parent_id` through to `render_handoff` so the handoff opening line matches.
- Update the "Backgrounded …" echo (line ~4209) to use `prefix` instead of
  `task_id_display(item_id)` for consistency.

### 4. `render_handoff` — `src/endless/task_cmd.py` (~3610)
- Add `parent_id: int | None = None` param.
- Build `label_prefix = _hierarchical_label_prefix(spawned_id, parent_id)` and add
  `"label_prefix": label_prefix` to `vars_payload`. (Falls back to `E-<id>` when
  `parent_id` is None, so existing non-bg callers keep working unchanged.)
- Update `show_handoff` (~3673): add `t.parent_id` to its SELECT and pass it
  through, so `endless task show --handoff` previews match dispatch output.

### 5. Handoff templates — `internal/templatecmd/templates/handoff/{task,bug,research,epic}.md.tmpl`
- Line 3 only: change `- E-{{.spawned_id}}: {{.title}}.` →
  `- {{.label_prefix}}: {{.title}}.`
- Leave every other `E-{{.spawned_id}}` reference intact (e.g. the
  `endless task show E-{{.spawned_id}} --text` lines) — those want the bare id.

### 6. Tests
- **Python** `tests/test_spawn_bg.py`: assert the dispatched `--name` carries the
  hierarchical label. Add a case for a parented task (`parent_id` set →
  `E-<parent>/E-<id>: <title>`) and a root task (`E-<id>: <title>`). The fixtures
  mock `claude`/`endless-go`; assert on the argv passed to `subprocess.run`.
- **Python** `tests/test_handoff.py`: add a case rendering with `parent_id` and
  assert the opening line contains `E-<parent>/E-<id>`; confirm the no-parent path
  still renders `E-<id>` (existing assertions should still hold).
- **Go** `internal/templatecmd/template_test.go`: add `"label_prefix"` to the
  payloads that render handoff templates (otherwise line 3 renders `<no value>`,
  since the renderer uses no `missingkey=error`). Add/adjust an assertion for the
  prefixed opening line.

## Out of scope
- Foreground tmux window naming (`_spawn_window_name`) — Agent View is the bg
  surface; not touched.
- Any Go-side port of the spawn/handoff DB reads (E-1486) — the path is already
  Python+`db.query`; this change only extends two existing SELECTs by one column.

## Verification
1. `just build` in the worktree (templates are embedded; rebuild `endless-go`).
2. `just test` — Python suite green, including the new spawn/handoff cases.
3. `go test ./internal/templatecmd/...` — Go template test green.
4. Manual handoff render for a child of an epic:
   ```sh
   endless task show E-1620 --handoff --db main   # opening line: E-1564/E-1620: ...
   ```
   and for a root/epic task confirm it stays `E-<id>: ...`.
5. Confirm dispatch label without launching a real agent: the new
   `test_spawn_bg.py` assertions verify the `--name` argv directly.

# E-1621 — `endless agents`: list bg agents scoped to the active epic

## Context
Claude Code's native Agent View is global — it can't filter background agents by
the epic you're coordinating. E-1621 adds a plain-text `endless agents` command
as the epic-scoped supplement (the TUI version is the `later` task E-1622).

The description specifies the query: background-agent sessions
(`kind_id=background`, `state='working'`) filtered by the resolved epic, printing
`id / short_id / task / title / started_at`. `--epic E-NNNN` overrides the
auto-resolved epic; `--all` drops the epic filter (project-scoped).

### Investigation finding (drives the design)
`active_epic_id` is written **only** for background-agent rows
(`RecordBgAgentSession`, session.go). Interactive/coordinator sessions —
the ones a person runs `endless agents` from — always have `active_epic_id NULL`,
because the claim handler `execTaskClaimed` (executor.go) sets only
`active_task_id`. E-1571 *intended* coordinator rows to carry the epic but
explicitly deferred that write to "the day-to-day claim flow," and it was never
implemented. Same gap also keeps the E-1571 status-line `[E-EEEE:E-CCCC]` prefix
from ever rendering for interactive sessions.

**Decisions (Mike):**
- Fill that gap **first**, in its own task/session; E-1621 then reads
  `active_epic_id` **literally**. → File the gap-fill task (cleans up E-1571);
  Mike spawns it separately. Block E-1621 on it.
- `--all` = **current project only** (project-scoped, not global).
- Interactive run with no `--epic`, no `--all`, no resolvable epic → **error
  with guidance** ("pass --epic E-NNNN or --all").

## Architecture
User surface is Python `endless agents`; the DB read is Go (no new Python DB
reads, per E-1486). Python resolves the current session id and shells to a new
`endless-go session-query list-bg-agents` verb that does the query and returns
JSON; Python formats plain text.

## Changes

### Go — `internal/monitor/bg_agents.go` (new)
- `type BgAgent struct { ID int64; ShortID string; TaskID *int64; Title string; StartedAt string }` (json-tagged).
- `ListBgAgentsForEpic(epicID int64) ([]BgAgent, error)` — `WHERE kind_id=background AND state='working' AND active_epic_id=?`, LEFT JOIN tasks for title, `ORDER BY started_at`.
- `ListBgAgentsForProject(projectID int64) ([]BgAgent, error)` — same but `project_id=?` (the `--all` path).
- `SessionActiveEpic(sessionID int64) (*int64, error)` — literal read of `active_epic_id` (nil when NULL / no row).
- Use `sessionkind.SessionKindBackground`, not a literal 2.

### Go — `internal/sessionquerycmd/session_query.go`
- Add `list-bg-agents` case + `runListBgAgents`; update `usage()`.
- Flags: `--session-id`, `--epic-id`, `--all`, `--project-root` (exactly one of the first three; `--all` needs `--project-root`).
- Returns JSON object: `{"scope":"epic"|"all","epic_id":<id|null>,"agents":[...]}`. For `--session-id`, resolves epic via `SessionActiveEpic`; null epic ⇒ `epic_id:null, agents:[]`.

### Python — `src/endless/agents_cmd.py` (new) + `cli.py`
- `@main.command("agents")` with `--epic` (TASK_ID type) and `--all`.
- Logic module (mirrors epic_cmd.py thin-wrapper style): validate not-both;
  resolve via `_current_endless_session_id` when neither flag; `config.require_db_context()` then shell to the Go verb with `config.go_db_context_args()`; parse JSON; format.
- Errors (Q3): no current session → guidance; scope==epic and epic_id null → guidance.
- Plain-text table: `Background agents under E-NNNN (N):` header, columns ID/SHORT/TASK/STARTED/TITLE; empty-state line.

## Tests
- Go: `internal/sessionquerycmd/list_bg_agents_test.go` — seed temp DB (bg agent under epic, a tmux session, an ended bg agent, a bg agent in another epic), invoke binary, assert JSON for `--epic-id`, `--session-id` (incl. null-epic), `--all`. Mirror `list_live_test.go`.
- Python: `tests/test_agents_cmd.py` — seed sessions+tasks, invoke `endless agents --epic`, assert rows + empty-state + both-flags error. Mirror `test_epic_cmd.py`.
- Per-task: `tests/tasks/e-1621-verify.sh` (sandbox DB; assert_succeeds/assert_refused), modeled on the E-1577 script.

## Follow-up task (filed, Mike spawns)
"Populate sessions.active_epic_id on interactive claim of an epic-descendant
task" — `--cleans-up E-1571`, `--relates-to E-1621`, `--parent E-1537`. Make
`execTaskClaimed` set `active_epic_id = nearestEpicAncestor(taskID)` (clear on
release / non-epic re-claim). Unblocks E-1621's interactive auto-resolve and the
status-line epic prefix. **E-1621 is blocked-by this task.**

## Verification
- `just build` then `just test` (Python) and `go test ./internal/...` (Go) green.
- `tests/tasks/e-1621-verify.sh` green against a sandbox DB.
- `--epic`/`--all` work immediately; interactive auto-resolve lights up once the
  gap-fill task lands.

# Populate sessions.active_epic_id on interactive task claim

## Context
E-1571 added `sessions.active_epic_id` and specified that a coordinator
(interactive/fg) session working under an epic should carry the epic's id in
`active_epic_id`, with `active_task_id` tracking the viewed child. It explicitly
deferred the *write* for interactive sessions out of its own scope ("part of
E-1570 and the day-to-day `endless task claim` flow"). That write was never
implemented.

Today `active_epic_id` is set **only** for background-agent rows
(`RecordBgAgentSession`, internal/monitor/session.go). The claim handler
`execTaskClaimed` (internal/events/executor.go) sets only `active_task_id`.
Consequences:
- The E-1571 status-line `[E-EEEE:E-CCCC]` / `[E-EEEE]` epic prefix can never
  render for interactive sessions (it branches on `active_epic_id`, always NULL).
- `endless agents` (E-1621) auto-resolves the active epic from the caller's
  `active_epic_id`, so the interactive auto path always errors until this lands.

## Change
In `execTaskClaimed` (internal/events/executor.go), when updating the session on
claim, also set `active_epic_id = nearestEpicAncestor(taskID)`:
- task has an epic ancestor → that epic id (an epic claimed directly resolves to
  itself, per `nearestEpicAncestor` depth-0 inclusion).
- no epic ancestor → NULL (clears any stale value from a prior claim).

`nearestEpicAncestor` (internal/monitor/session.go) is currently unexported
in `monitor`. Either export it (e.g. `NearestEpicAncestor`) for the events
package, or inline the same recursive-CTE resolution in the executor's UPDATE as
a correlated subquery:

```sql
UPDATE sessions
   SET active_task_id = ?,
       active_epic_id = (
         WITH RECURSIVE ancestry(id, parent_id, type_id, depth) AS (
           SELECT id, parent_id, type_id, 0 FROM tasks WHERE id = ?
           UNION ALL
           SELECT t.id, t.parent_id, t.type_id, a.depth+1
             FROM tasks t JOIN ancestry a ON t.id = a.parent_id
         )
         SELECT a.id FROM ancestry a
           JOIN task_types tt ON tt.id = a.type_id
          WHERE tt.slug = 'epic'
          ORDER BY a.depth LIMIT 1
       )
 WHERE id = ?
```

The single-statement subquery avoids exporting the helper and keeps the write
atomic. Pick whichever fits the executor's existing style (it uses raw SQL via
`db.Exec`).

Also handle release: `execTaskReleased` (executor.go) NULLs `active_task_id`;
it should NULL `active_epic_id` too, so a released coordinator session doesn't
keep a stale epic.

## Tests
- Extend `internal/events` tests: claim a child of an epic → row has
  `active_epic_id` = epic; claim a standalone task → NULL; claim the epic
  directly → its own id; release → both NULL.
- Confirm the status-line prefix now renders for an interactive session (an
  existing `tmux_lookup`/`status_line` test seeded with `active_epic_id`).

## Verification
- `go test ./internal/events/... ./internal/monitor/...` green.
- Manually: `endless task claim <epic-child>` then check the session row's
  `active_epic_id`; `endless agents` (E-1621) interactive auto-resolve now works.

## Relations
- Cleans up E-1571 (implements its deferred coordinator-write design).
- Relates to E-1621 (which is blocked-by this task).

Add an Analysis section to task show plus an --all-fields flag, and fix the validator help text that wrongly steers long-form analysis to --text.

# E-1628 — Fix worktree land mis-targeting the sandbox DB from a self-dev session

## Context
Discovered while landing E-1542 from a Claude session spawned inside a self-dev
worktree: `just land` failed at the `task.landed` step with a `task_landings`
FK error (787), and only succeeded once `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` was forced to the real
config dir. The landing is a real/main operation, but it was targeting the
per-worktree sandbox DB.

## Root cause (verified 2026-06-23)
The `just land` recipe runs three separate `endless` processes — `endless db
backup`, `endless db apply-change <f>` (per added change file), and `endless
worktree land <id>` (Justfile `land` recipe, ~lines 208-220). None pass `--db`,
so each inherits the invoking shell's `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. A Claude session spawned
inside a self-dev worktree has that XDG pointed at the sandbox
(`~/.cache/endless/sandboxes/e-NNN`, injected by the worktree's
`.claude/settings.json`), so all three target the **sandbox** DB.

But landing is inherently a real/main operation: the landed task lives only in
the real DB, schema changes belong to the real DB, and the merge is into `main`.
Hard failure: the `task.landed` emit's `task_landings` insert violates the
`task_id` FK because the task isn't in the sandbox; schema-apply also silently
records its `_schema_version` marker in the sandbox. Confirmed fix signal: with
`XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$HOME/.config` the land succeeds end-to-end.

## Fix
Make the land-flow infrastructure commands default to the **real/main DB** when
no explicit `--db` was given — they are "always-main" operations, the Python
analogue of the Go-side `PinMainDB` for hook/channel/tmux (E-1450/E-1429).

At each command's entry, if `config.RESOLVED_CONFIG_DIR is None`, call
`config.apply_db_choice("main")` (it pins `config.main_config_dir()` via
`set_db_context`, so Python reads use the real `DB_PATH` **and**
`go_db_context_args()` then threads `--config-dir <real>` to every downstream
`endless-go` shellout). An explicit `--db main|sandbox` is honored — only force
when unset.

Command entry points to pin:
- `endless worktree land` (`src/endless/cli.py` → `land_worktree` in `worktree_cmd.py`)
- `endless db apply-change`
- `endless db backup`

Putting the default in the commands (not the `just land` recipe) keeps both
`just land` and direct `endless worktree land` invocations correct, so the
behavior ships in the product, not the dev wrapper (per "just is dev-only" /
"ship behavior in product, not machine config").

**Alternative considered & rejected:** have the `just land` recipe pass `--db
main` to its three `endless` calls. Smaller, but leaves direct `endless worktree
land` / `endless db apply-change` invocations exposed and pushes load-bearing
behavior into the dev wrapper instead of the command.

## Out of scope / notes
- E-1474 already made the post-ff-merge `task.landed` emit re-runnable (symptom
  tolerance); this fixes the root cause so the emit doesn't fail to begin with.
- The session resolver returned a sandbox session id (`2`) rather than the
  real-DB id (`722`) from the main checkout. Once the land pins main, session
  resolution also runs against the real DB; confirm during implementation and
  file separately if it persists.

## Tests
- Python unit: invoke `land_worktree` (and the `db apply-change` / `db backup`
  entries) with `RESOLVED_CONFIG_DIR=None` and a sandbox-pointing XDG; assert
  each pins `main_config_dir()` (RESOLVED_CONFIG_DIR becomes the real dir;
  `go_db_context_args()` threads `--config-dir <real>`). Assert an explicit
  `--db sandbox` is NOT overridden.
- Per-task verify script `tests/tasks/e-1628-verify.sh`: from a sandbox-routed
  env (XDG=sandbox, no `--db`), land a throwaway real-DB task and assert the
  `task_landings` row is written to the **real** DB and the FK passes —
  reproducing E-1542's failure on baseline and confirming the fix.

## Critical files
- `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py` (`land_worktree` entry)
- `src/endless/cli.py` (`worktree_land`, `db apply-change`, `db backup` registrations)
- `src/endless/config.py` (reuse `apply_db_choice` / `main_config_dir` / `set_db_context`; no change expected)

## Verification
From a Claude session inside a self-dev worktree (XDG=sandbox), run `just land
E-NNN` with **no** XDG override: the landing records to the real DB, the
`task_landings` FK passes, and `_schema_version` markers land in the real DB.

# E-1640 — Fix duplicate session rows minted per Claude launch when TMUX_PANE is empty

**Independent (parent of E-1641).** Full evidence in this task's `analysis` field. · **Layer:** Go

## Root cause (recap)
Dedup key is `sessions.session_id` (the Claude UUID), not `active_task_id`. Every launch gets a
new UUID, so SessionStart's upsert finds no conflict and **INSERTs a new row** via `TouchSession`
(`internal/monitor/session.go`, from `internal/hookcmd/claude.go`) and `InitSession`
(`session.go`). The only intended dedup — collision-invalidation by `process` (tmux pane),
`session.go` — is **inert** because `TMUX_PANE` is empty: `process` is NULL on 728/744
rows and `COALESCE(NULLIF(excluded.process,''))` refuses to store an empty pane. Sub-10s ghosts accrue.

## Files
- `internal/monitor/session.go`: `TouchSession` (220-295), `InitSession` (104-121), collision
  invalidation (280-292), `BindSessionToTask` (38-60).
- `internal/hookcmd/claude.go`: SessionStart ordering (154-180), `TouchSession` call (~161).

## Approach — active_task_id-scoped fallback dedup for the empty-pane case
When `process` is empty **and** `active_task_id` is known, fold into the existing recent
non-ended row for that task instead of inserting a fresh-UUID row:
- **Task known at SessionStart?** For spawned sessions yes (`@endless_task_id` window var read by
  the hook). Confirm binding order: if `BindSessionToTask` runs *after* `TouchSession`, move/peek
  the task id earlier or run the fallback on the bind step.
- **Fold rule:** if a non-ended row exists for the same `active_task_id` with empty `process` and
  recent `last_activity`, reuse it (update `session_id` + `last_activity`) rather than INSERT.
  Scope tightly (same task + empty process + recent) so two genuinely concurrent sessions aren't merged.
- **Ad-hoc (unbound) sessions:** task unknown → still create a row (real session until bound).

## Verification — create a per-task verify script
Create `tests/tasks/e-1640-verify.sh` in the `e-1624-verify.sh` shape (bash, `set -u`, the
`section`/`report_*`/`summary` helpers, `cd` repo root, ensure `go.work`, exit 0/1/2). Drive the
REAL code path via Go tests in `internal/monitor` — don't re-implement dedup logic.

The script asserts (named checks):
- `internal/monitor` compiles (`go build ./internal/monitor/`).
- A Go test (`go test -count=1 -run ^TestTouchSession_FoldsEmptyPaneSameTask$ ./internal/monitor/`)
  drives repeated `TouchSession` with empty `process` + the same `active_task_id` and asserts the
  row count stays **1** (folds), not N.
- A second Go test asserts a genuinely separate, freshly-claimed session on the same task is **NOT**
  folded into the stale row.
- `internal/monitor` full suite stays green (`go test -count=1 ./internal/monitor/`).

Re-runnability (sandbox/test DB):
- Tests build their own schema-applied DB and derive ids freshly — never hardcode a UNIQUE
  `session_id`/`short_id`; use fresh per-run values.
- Run the script at least TWICE before declaring it done.

## Implemented (2026-06-29) — decisions confirmed with Mike

The original "fold/reuse the row (update `session_id`)" wording above was **not**
used. Two decisions changed it:

1. **Mechanism = end stale rows, not mutate `session_id`.** Mutating a surviving
   row's `session_id` is FK-unsafe in production: `session_messages.session_id`
   REFERENCES `sessions(session_id)` ON DELETE CASCADE only (no ON UPDATE), so
   the update throws `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` whenever the fold target has
   any messages — and there is no migration path to add ON UPDATE CASCADE
   (schema.sql `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` can't alter existing DBs; the
   V-migration framework was removed). Instead: keep the new-UUID row, and in
   `BindSessionToTask` end any OTHER non-ended foreground (`kind_id` = tmux) row
   for the same `active_task_id` that has no pane. FK-safe (only `state` changes),
   mirrors the existing collision-invalidation idiom.
2. **No recency window.** End all prior matching rows regardless of
   `last_activity` age. A resume can happen long after the prior row went idle, so
   a recency window would miss that duplicate; concurrency-merge is prevented by
   worktree locks (one live foreground session per task) plus the `kind_id` guard
   that excludes background agents.

**Code:** `internal/monitor/session.go` `BindSessionToTask` — bind upsert +
scoped invalidation now run in one transaction. All bind paths (spawn-marker
auto-bind, `autoBindFromCwd`, `StartWorkSession`) route through it.

**Tests:** `internal/monitor/session_dedup_test.go` —
`TestBindSessionToTask_EndsStalePanelessRowsSameTask`,
`_RepeatedLaunchesStayAtOneLiveRow`, `_DoesNotEndBackgroundAgentSameTask`,
`_DoesNotEndPanedRowSameTask`, `_DoesNotEndOtherTasksRows`. (Named for the actual
bind-step mechanism, not the plan's `TestTouchSession_Folds*`.)

**Verify-handoff — tell the user to verify with (only) this:**
```
esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1640-verify.sh
```
fields.analysis:
Researched 2026-06-24 against the 744-row sessions table.

ROOT CAUSE: dedup key is sessions.session_id (Claude UUID), not active_task_id. Every Claude launch (resume / respawn / aborted spawn / /clear) has a new UUID, so SessionStart's upsert finds no conflict and INSERTs a new row via TouchSession (internal/monitor/session.go, called from internal/hookcmd/claude.go) and InitSession (session.go). The intended dedup -- collision-invalidation by process/tmux-pane (session.go) -- is INERT because TMUX_PANE is empty in the hook env: process is NULL on 728/744 rows and COALESCE(NULLIF(excluded.process,'')) refuses to store an empty pane, so there is no pane to collide on.

EVIDENCE: Pattern-A ghost rows (ended, NULL process, no session_statuses, <10s) = 298 DB-wide under the loose filter; 37 under the strict prune criteria (kind_id=1, not-newest-per-task). Examples: task 894 = three 4-9s rows; task 1362 = one real row (id 490) + five sub-10s ghosts.

DISPROVEN: bg-agent double-insert -- decorate-before-touch ordering at claude.go is correct (DecorateBgSession UPDATEs by short_id before TouchSession); all sampled target rows are kind_id=1.

FIX: add an active_task_id-scoped fallback dedup for the empty-pane case so SessionStart folds into / reuses the most-recent non-ended row for the same task instead of inserting a fresh-UUID row.

Other refs: session.go BindSessionToTask, :341-375 RecordBgAgentSession, :447-465 DecorateBgSession; claude.go decorate->touch->init ordering, :296-298 EndSession (SessionEnd, rarely fires).

# Diagnosis: why the endless status row vanishes on /bg + claude attach

## Root cause

The row is **not** removed. `status` stays `2` and `status-format[1]` stays the endless line
through the whole flow (live capture: the after-attach step was identical to before except `$TMUX`
was **empty**; `@server_uuid` and the `$TMUX` server PID were unchanged — no tmux restart, no
config re-source). The failure is in **pane → session → task resolution**:

1. `/bg` moves the session to a **detached Claude daemon** (`claude daemon run --origin transient`)
   as a `--bg-pty-host` child. After `claude attach`, the session's hooks fire from that daemon with
   **no `$TMUX` / `$TMUX_PANE`** — there is no tmux pane anywhere in the process lineage. (The
   viewing pane belongs to the separate `claude attach` *client* process.)
2. The endless hook keys all pane identity off `os.Getenv("TMUX_PANE")`
   (`internal/hookcmd/claude.go` TouchSession; also :975/:1005/:1049/:1260). With it empty,
   `TouchSession`'s `NULLIF(?, '')` records the reattached session with **`process=NULL`** — no pane
   binding — and it has no task.
3. The status-line printer (`status-format[1]`) is invoked by tmux with the real focused pane id and
   resolves pane→session→active_task via `sessions.process` (`internal/monitor/tmux_lookup.go`
   `GetActiveTaskForPane`). The paneless daemon session is unreachable that way.
4. The row keeps rendering only while the **prior** in-pane session row still maps that pane→task.
   Once that stale row is invalidated (collision invalidation when a later event carries the pane,
   `ReapDeadTmuxPanes`, or it ends), the pane resolves to the paneless/taskless reattached row →
   placeholder/hint → the row "vanishes and does not re-render" (every later bg event still has an
   empty `$TMUX_PANE`).

Live evidence: parent in-pane session `81f9df34` (task E-1564, `process=%38`) vs. the reattached
daemon session (paneless, taskless). The printer still showed `[E-1564]…` only because the stale
parent row coincidentally still held `%38`.

**Both originally-considered fixes are invalid:** re-running `endless tmux apply` is a no-op
(`status`/`status-format[1]` are intact), and recovering the pane from PID/TTY ancestry is
structurally impossible (a `/bg` session has no tmux pane to recover).

## Verified facts about the Claude bg/daemon model

- `/bg` mints a **new session UUID** (`ec7cb9e1` → `24126b24`); reattach keeps the new id. No
  recorded old→new link in job dir, transcript metadata, or env.
- bg sessions **do** fire endless hooks and get DB rows (paneless, taskless).
- bg session env signals: `CLAUDE_JOB_DIR=~/.claude/jobs/<bg-short-id>` and
  `CLAUDE_ENABLE_STREAM_WATCHDOG=1`; transcript entries carry `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1` and a
  `sessionKind` field (the child knows it is a child, not who its parent is).
- The `claude attach <short-id>` client runs in a tmux pane (has `$TMUX_PANE`, id in argv) but does
  **not** fire an endless hook. Its parent is interactive `-zsh`, so Mike's `claude` shell function
  intercepts it (wrapper reach confirmed).

## Key discovery — the automatic parent→child bridge

`/bg` **copies the full parent conversation into the child transcript with message uuids preserved**,
then appends new ones (measured: all 13 parent uuids present in the child, + 11 new). endless already
persists these in `session_messages(session_id, message_uuid)` with `message_uuid` globally
`UNIQUE` — so a bg child's parent is identifiable by uuid lookup, with **no schema change**. This is
what makes automatic task/epic inheritance across `/bg` possible (see the bug task's fix plan).

# E-1653: Fix tasks stranded on old status slugs (no-compromise, no-footgun)

## Context

E-1252 renamed the task-status vocabulary in **code + docs only** —
`needs_plan→unplanned`, `in_progress→underway`, `verify→unverified` — and
deliberately left the **data** and the **immutable ledger** on the old slugs.
The new code no longer recognizes the old slugs, so **424 live tasks**
(330 `needs_plan` + 19 `in_progress` + 75 `verify`) fall out of the queries that
compute "active"/filters (e.g. `internal/monitor/task.go` and
`internal/web/queries.go` select `status IN ('unplanned','ready','underway')`).
Result: `endless task active`, `next`, and `list --status` under-report.

The original E-1653 plan (2026-06-25) also proposed **rewriting the committed
ledger** (perl) plus a cross-worktree pre-land alignment script. That is
superseded by **E-1652** (completed 2026-06-28), whose locked design is: never
rewrite the committed ledger — map old values → new at **replay** time via
upcasting. E-1652 notes the codebase **already does ad-hoc upcasting** for
decisions (`mapLegacyDecisionStatus`) and that E-1671 (the full pipeline) will
**consolidate such shims as seed entries**.

**Decisions locked with Mike this session:**
- Do **not** rewrite the ledger — not even once ("dormant drift is a footgun").
- Instead close the footgun with a small **projector shim** (the E-1652-endorsed
  ad-hoc seed entry), so a future `rebuild-db`/`validate-db` maps old→new and
  live == replayed. No rewrite, no drift.
- Add the `unapproved` status now — **Python lists only**; web UI is not a
  priority (its status surfaces stay for E-1648, which owns the approval workflow).

Scope note: this does **not** make `rebuild-db` safe — it independently drops
~233 tasks (E-1654's job). The shim closes only the *status-revert* footgun.

## Change 1 — Live-DB projection fix (the immediate unstranding)

New change-file `internal/schema/changes/e-1653-migrate-status-data.sql`
(named for E-1653, the task doing it — the plan's `e-1252-…` name is wrong by
convention). Header comment documents that this is **projection-only** (ledger
intentionally untouched; the projector shim in Change 2 handles replay):

```sql
UPDATE tasks SET status = CASE status
    WHEN 'needs_plan'  THEN 'unplanned'
    WHEN 'in_progress' THEN 'underway'
    WHEN 'verify'      THEN 'unverified'
END
WHERE status IN ('needs_plan', 'in_progress', 'verify');
```

`blocked` intentionally untouched (E-1532 drops it). Apply to the **live** DB:

1. `endless db backup --db main`  (safety net first)
2. `endless db apply-change internal/schema/changes/e-1653-migrate-status-data.sql --db main`

`apply-change` wraps the file in `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, records a `_schema_version`
marker, and is idempotent — so re-applying at land time (`just land` drives
change-files) is a no-op. The sandbox never applies change-files (it builds from
`schema.sql`), so this only ever runs against the real DB.

## Change 2 — Projector shim `mapLegacyTaskStatus` (closes the footgun)

Mirror the existing `mapLegacyDecisionStatus` (`internal/events/decision.go`).
Add to `internal/events/projector.go` a **pass-through-default** mapper:

```go
func mapLegacyTaskStatus(legacy string) string {
	switch legacy {
	case "needs_plan":
		return "unplanned"
	case "in_progress":
		return "underway"
	case "verify":
		return "unverified"
	default:
		return legacy   // open status set — pass through unchanged
	}
}
```

(Default must pass through — unlike the decision mapper — because task statuses
are an open set; only the three retired slugs are remapped. `blocked`,
`completed`, `declined`, `obsolete` etc. flow untouched.)

Insert a call at the **four** replay handlers that write `tasks.status` from the
payload (map into a local *before* the SQL write and before any terminal-status
check that reads the value):

- `replayTaskCreated` — wrap `p.Status` (~line 178). (Genuine tasks only;
  `type=="decision"` already routes away at ~133.)
- `replayTaskStatusChanged` — map `p.NewStatus` into a local right after
  `taskID := …` (~line 238); reused at the terminal check (~242), cascade
  UPDATE (~255), and single-row UPDATE (~263).
- `replayTaskFieldsUpdated` — map the `status` field value where appended
  (~368-369) and feed the mapped value into the terminal check (~372-390).
- `replayEpicStatusDerived` — wrap `p.NewStatus` (~line 525).

`replayTaskImported` needs no change (hardcodes `'unplanned'`, ignores payload).
`task.claimed`/`task.released` carry no status.

**Tests** in `internal/events/projector_test.go` (extend the existing
`TestProjectToTempDB_TaskCreatedProducesRow` analog at line 34): add cases that
feed a legacy slug through each of the four paths and assert the projected
`tasks.status` is the new slug. Add an epic case near
`epic_derivation_test.go`.

## Change 3 — Add `unapproved` to the valid status set (Python only)

Insert `unapproved` right after `unplanned` (its workflow position: unplanned →
unapproved → ready) in both:
- `src/endless/cli.py` — `TASK_STATUSES`.
- `src/endless/task_cmd.py` — the `valid` tuple.

Do **not** touch terminal/reopenable sets or the active-task queries — `unapproved`
is a pre-`ready` gate with no rows and no `approve` verb yet; E-1648 wires the
workflow. Do **not** touch the Go web surfaces (`internal/web/handlers.go` valid
map, `status_detail.templ` `statusChoices`) — web UI deferred per Mike.

## Files

- `internal/schema/changes/e-1653-migrate-status-data.sql` (new)
- `internal/events/projector.go` (add `mapLegacyTaskStatus` + 4 call sites)
- `internal/events/projector_test.go` (+ `epic_derivation_test.go`) — shim tests
- `src/endless/cli.py`, `src/endless/task_cmd.py` — add `unapproved`
- `tests/tasks/e-1653-verify.sh` (new) — per-task verify script (sandbox-side)

## Build & test

- `just build` (regenerates templ, builds Go into `bin/`) — required so the
  worktree binary reflects the projector change.
- `go test ./internal/events/...` — new shim cases pass.
- `just test` — Python suite green (check nothing asserts `len(TASK_STATUSES)`;
  `tests/tasks/e-1252-verify.sh` should still pass).

## Verification (end to end)

1. **Live unstranding** — `endless sql "SELECT status,COUNT(*) FROM tasks GROUP BY status" --db main`:
   zero `needs_plan`/`in_progress`/`verify`; `unplanned`/`underway`/`unverified`
   up by 330/19/75; total still **1002**.
2. `endless task active --db main` now returns the real in-progress/verify set,
   not the undercount.
3. **Footgun disarmed** — `go test ./internal/events/...`: replaying a legacy
   slug through each of the 4 paths yields the new slug (live == replayed on the
   status axis; no rewrite of the ledger).
4. **`unapproved` accepted** — in the sandbox (don't pollute main):
   `endless task update <id> --status unapproved --db sandbox` succeeds.
5. Backup exists under `~/.config/endless/backups/`.

## Landing

Commit all changes to the worktree branch. Set `endless task update E-1653
--status unverified --db main`. Spawning session (E-1687) owns `just land E-1653`;
the change-file re-applies as a no-op via its `_schema_version` marker. No ledger
rewrite ⇒ no cross-worktree rebase conflict surface.

fields.analysis: Schema: each verb gets 'category' (usually one of action|investigation; allow a short multi-set for genuine duals like 'compare'). Each task type declares 'accepts: [categories]' (task/bug/chore -> [action]; research/brainstorm -> [investigation]). Validity(verb,type) = type.accepts contains verb.category. GATE at task creation: block on mismatch; prefer giving a dual verb BOTH categories over a justification bypass (bypasses get taken). Touch-points: src/endless/matchers.py (defaults + is_completable_verb -> category lookup), .endless/verbs.jsonl, cli.py (current completable check), wherever task types are defined (locate first), and 'endless verb' (set/show category). NOTE completable's current VALUES are correct (knowledge-type verbs whose tasks reach 'completed') -- this generalizes, not corrects. The --justification requirement on --type research is a separate per-type policy, out of scope. COORDINATION: a 'brainstorm' type + its accepts entry are being added in a parallel session touching the same type registry; sequence edits to avoid collision.

fields.description: The E-1538/E-1571/E-1542 task_types/session_kinds/gate_kinds integrity checks (internal/monitor/db.go) fail closed, but 'endless-go hook claude' surfaces the failure with a generic non-zero exit, which Claude Code treats as a NON-BLOCKING PostToolUse error: shown to the USER only, never injected into the agent's context (only exit code 2 is fed to the model on PostToolUse). So agents cannot honor 'STOP on errors' for hook/DB failures -- they never see them. DECIDED (Mike): ALWAYS block on integrity failure -- exit 2 from the hook so the agent halts; NO grace window for transient cross-session migration windows (a hard stop while a schema settles is correct and avoids hard-to-unravel ripple effects). Touch-points in analysis.

# E-1661 — Hook blocks (exit 2) on integrity/DB failure

Implements ED-1519. Decided (Mike): ALWAYS block, no grace window.

## Steps
1. Confirm Claude Code PostToolUse semantics: exit code 2 feeds stderr to the
   model (agent sees it); any other non-zero is user-only ("non-blocking status
   code"). Use the claude-code-guide agent if unsure.
2. internal/hookcmd/claude.go, the `hook claude` path: when project lookup /
   DB Open() returns an integrity or DB-open error (from internal/monitor/db.go
   VerifyIntegrity, db.go), exit **2** with the error on stderr, instead
   of the current non-blocking exit. Apply to every hook event that opens the DB
   (PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart).
3. Keep the message actionable: name the drifted table and the stale-binary
   remedy (rebuild/reinstall).

## Non-goals
No grace window, no transient tolerance (ED-1519). A hard stop while a schema
settles is the intended behavior.

## Verify (tests/tasks/e-1661-verify.sh)
- Seed a temp DB whose task_types drifts from the enum; run the hook binary
  against it; assert exit code == 2 AND stderr contains "integrity check".
- Healthy DB: hook exits 0.

fields.analysis: Current auto-provision (_maybe_auto_sandbox_bind, worktree_cmd.py) already invokes 'endless-go sandbox init/bind' -- PRODUCT-compliant, NOT just; extend that pattern. Gap: it never builds the worktree binaries (no bin/) nor installs the hook override, so hook + CLI run the global binary. PRODUCT: invoke a project-declared provision script, never 'just' from shipped code. Coordinate with E-1368 (replaces bin-sandbox wrappers with binary self-detect) so this doesn't entrench bin-sandbox. Touch-points: _maybe_auto_sandbox_bind, the 'endless-go sandbox' subcommands, .endless/config.json (declare provision script), task_cmd.py claim/spawn.

# E-1664 — A self_dev land always uses the worktree's endless-go binary

## Context

E-1660 fixed `just land` tripping the `task_types` integrity gate when a branch
ADDS a mirrored-enum value (a new `task_types` row): the land applies the schema
change with the worktree binary, then `endless worktree land` emits the
`task.landed` event. Under `--db main` (pinned by `default_db_to_main()`, E-1628),
`_resolve_endless_go()` resolves the **global** `endless-go` via `shutil.which` —
which `just build` hasn't refreshed yet, so its `tasktype` enum lacks the new
constant and `monitor.DB()`'s `VerifyIntegrity` fails closed, forcing a manual
`just install && just land` recovery.

E-1660's fix was a per-shellout PATH-prepend in the Justfile recipe — fragile:
every `endless-go` shellout must individually be pointed at the worktree binary,
and the next one added can silently forget.

## Core insight (the design driver)

Binary selection during a land is **not a choice** the way `--db main|sandbox`
is. `--db` picks between two valid targets. The executable has exactly **one**
correct value during a self_dev land: the **worktree's** binary — it is the
candidate-under-development, and because the land applies the schema change
first, it is the only binary whose embedded schema/enums match the rows just
written. The global is by construction the not-yet-refreshed one mid-land.

So this is an **invariant, not a parameter**: a self_dev land uses the worktree
binary, full stop. No flag, no env var, no override surface. (An env var was
rejected — it leaks across inherited environments into the wrong context, and
`_resolve_endless_go` runs on every schema-mutating shellout. A flag was rejected
— selection isn't a choice to expose.)

**Missing-binary edge → loud error, not silent global fallback.** E-1660's only
use of the global was a silent fallback when the worktree binary was absent.
E-1662 shows that exact fallback is a bug-source ("...fall back to the GLOBAL
binary... this is also what left e-1643 exposed to the stale-global-binary
integrity skew"). So an absent worktree binary during a self_dev land is a loud
failure ("worktree not built — run `just build`"), enforcing the self_dev
"exercise candidate code" invariant. A *fully reaped* worktree can't be landed
anyway — `git worktree` won't list it, so `land_worktree` fails at
`_branch_for_task` before any binary is needed. No legitimate global-fallback
path remains. (Slightly stricter than strictly necessary for a no-schema-change
land where the global would also work — but that strictness is aligned with
E-1662: an unbuilt self_dev worktree is a bug to surface, not mask.)

## Approach

### 1. `_resolve_endless_go()` gains an explicit `override` parameter

`src/endless/event_bridge.py` — `def _resolve_endless_go(override: str | None
= None)`. When `override` is given, validate it is a file and executable; return
it; raise a loud `click.ClickException` naming the path (`~`-relative via the
existing lines 39-42 helper) if invalid. When `None`, existing behavior is
unchanged (`resolved_worktree_endless_go()` → `shutil.which`). Pure internal
plumbing — no env, no CLI surface.

### 2. Thread it through the land's emit only

- `emit_event(...)` (event_bridge.py) gains `endless_go_bin: str | None =
  None`, passed to `_resolve_endless_go(override=endless_go_bin)`.
- `_record_landing(...)` (worktree_cmd.py:~1264, the land's emit wrapper) gains
  `endless_go_bin` and forwards it to `emit_event`.
- `apply_change` / `backup_db` are **untouched** (separate top-level Justfile
  invocations; out of E-1664 scope — see "Left alone" below).

### 3. `land_worktree` computes the invariant via a testable helper

Add a small seam so the script can assert this without standing up a full land:

`src/endless/worktree_cmd.py` — `def _resolve_land_endless_go(worktree_path:
Path, project_root: Path) -> str | None:` returns `None` for a non-self_dev
project (`config.project_is_self_dev(project_root)` is False ⇒ global, unchanged);
otherwise computes `worktree_path / "bin" / "endless-go"`, and if it is not a
file / not executable raises a loud `click.ClickException` ("self_dev worktree
isn't built — run `just build` in the worktree before landing"), else returns its
`str`. `land_worktree` (line 1306), past the dry-run guard, calls this helper and
passes the result as `endless_go_bin` to `_record_landing`. The three branches
(self_dev+present → path, self_dev+missing → loud error, non-self_dev → None) are
exactly what e-1664-verify.sh exercises.

### 4. Justfile: remove E-1660's PATH-prepend AND its guard

`justfile:166` land recipe — the `if [ -x "$wt/bin/endless-go" ]; then PATH=…
endless worktree land …; else …; fi` block becomes a plain
`endless worktree land "$tid"`. The product code now enforces the worktree binary
for self_dev lands and fails loudly if unbuilt.

## Files to modify

- `src/endless/event_bridge.py` — `override` param + validation in
  `_resolve_endless_go`; `endless_go_bin` param on `emit_event`; docstrings.
- `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py` — `_resolve_land_endless_go` helper; call it in
  `land_worktree`; `endless_go_bin` thread through `_record_landing`.
- `justfile` — plain land call (drop E-1660 block).
- `tests/tasks/e-1664-verify.sh` — **the single verification surface** (deliverable;
  ad-hoc reference-style, modeled on `tests/tasks/e-1660-verify.sh` — NOT the
  E-1596 `verify.toml` system the other session is building).

## Left alone / out of scope (with reasons, not silent)

- **apply-change / backup E-1510 PATH-prepends** stay. They are separate
  processes, so no per-invocation mechanism can be "set once" across them; true
  set-once de-fragilization only comes from consolidating the land steps into one
  process — the deferred **project-configurable land hook**, which belongs in the
  existing **extension-model family** (E-1014 shipped `.endless/extensions/use.sh`;
  E-1086 worktree-init hook; E-1188 the three-tier model design). Captured there,
  not built here.
- **E-1613** (add `ENDLESS_GO_BIN` env override to `_resolve_endless_go` so
  verify scripts can pin the artifact-under-test) should be **marked obsolete**.
  Both its halves are dead: (a) its env-var mechanism is exactly the leakage
  approach rejected here; (b) its only concrete driver is already solved — the
  verify-suite scripts (e.g. `tests/tasks/e-1660-verify.sh`) invoke the worktree
  binary by absolute path (`WT_BIN="$REPO_ROOT/bin/endless-go"`), bypassing
  `_resolve_endless_go` entirely and already loud-erroring if unbuilt. Nothing
  remains for the override to add. E-1664's `override` param is internal land
  plumbing, not a verify-script surface, so it neither implements nor revives
  E-1613.

## Verification

The verification is a single committed script. The handoff to Mike is exactly:

```
esu
./tests/tasks/e-1664-verify.sh
```

`tests/tasks/e-1664-verify.sh` (self-contained; builds/asserts the worktree
binary itself, isolates via temp `HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` + a schema-seeded DB,
invokes the worktree `endless-go` by absolute path, prints pass/fail per check +
a summary, exits 0 all-pass / 1 any-fail / 2 setup error). Checks:

- **Gate still armed (not weakened):** an emit against a DB carrying a phantom
  `task_types` row with no enum constant MUST fail with the exact integrity error
  (matched case-accurately per E-1596's lesson).
- **Matching-enum clears the gate:** the same emit against a clean schema-seeded
  DB gets past integrity.
- **Override honored:** `_resolve_endless_go(override=<valid>)` returns it;
  `override=<missing/non-exec>` raises a loud error; `override=None` ⇒ unchanged
  global/sandbox resolution (Python one-liners via `uv run`).
- **Land invariant:** `_resolve_land_endless_go` returns the worktree binary path
  when self_dev + present, raises the loud "not built" error when self_dev +
  missing, returns `None` for a non-self_dev project.
- **Justfile regression guard:** the `land` recipe invokes `endless worktree land
  "$tid"` plainly — no `PATH="$wt/bin:…"` wrapper and no E-1660 guard block

## Ledger coordination (post-implementation, confirm with Mike)

- E-1664 already `cleans_up` E-1660.
- Mark **E-1613 obsolete** with a note recording why (env approach rejected;
  verify scripts pin the binary by absolute path, bypassing `_resolve_endless_go`).
  It sits under E-1596, so confirm the disposition with Mike; exact verb/status
  resolved against `endless guide` at implementation time.
- Optionally note the land-hook requirement against E-1188 (extension model) so
  the apply-change consolidation has a tracked home — confirm before editing his

# E-1681 — `endless session goto` / `session back` (tmux session navigation)

## Context

The `session next` view (E-1465) lists in-flight sessions as `⟳` rows keyed by the
task each is working, but there's no way to jump tmux focus to one, and a spawned
session's only way "home" is the literal `tmux switch-client -t %NNN` baked into
its handoff. This task adds:

- `endless session goto <task|session>` — switch the tmux client's focus to the
  target session's pane.
- `endless session back` — return browser-style via a back-stack.

## Design (decided with Mike)

Two concerns were separated:
1. **Back-stack** (drives `back`) — ephemeral, server-life navigation state. **In
   scope here.**
2. **Durable navigation trail** (analysis / recovering a lost session, captures
   manual moves too) — **out of scope; filed as a follow-up** (`--cleans-up E-1681`).

### Back-stack
- **Storage:** a **tmux server option**, keyed per attached client:
  `@endless_backstack_<sanitized client_name>` (value = space-separated tokens,
  top of stack = last token). Falls back to a global `@endless_backstack` when no
  client name is resolvable. Lifetime matches the tmux server, which is exactly as
  long as the pane ids inside it are valid. No file, no DB, no schema change.
  (Sessions writes are Go-only and tmux options are already read/written from
  Python — `@endless_spawned_by`, `@endless_session_uuid` — so this is the
  least-machinery right-sized tool for ephemeral nav state.)
- **Unit = endless session id**, not raw pane (Mike's point: panes are volatile,
  a spawner can restart into a new pane under the same session id). A stack token
  is a session id (digits) resolved to its *current* live pane at pop-time. A
  source location that isn't a tracked session (e.g. a plain shell pane) is stored
  as a raw pane id (`%NNN`) and used directly — the leading `%` distinguishes the
  two token kinds.
- **Scope = the navigator = the attached tmux client.** For a single-terminal
  setup this coincides with "global per tmux server."
- **Capture = `goto` only** (predictable: `back` undoes your last `goto`; manual
  `select-window` moves don't touch it — capturing those belongs to the durable
  trail follow-up).

### `session goto <ref>`
1. Require tmux (`$TMUX`); else friendly error.
2. Resolve `<ref>` → target session → its live pane (rules below); friendly error
   on no-match / ambiguous / no-live-session.
3. Resolve the current pane (`$TMUX_PANE`) → its session id if tracked, else keep
   the raw pane id; push that token onto this client's stack.
4. `tmux switch-client -t <target-pane>`. If the target pane is gone, error and
   pop the token we just pushed (don't leave it dangling).
5. Status to stderr: `• goto E-NNNN → session E-MM (pane %214)`.

Ref resolution (reusing the Go-backed `_live_sessions` read — no new Go):
- `E-NNNN` → task id → live sessions with that `active_task_id`, most recent
  (`last_activity DESC`, already the Go order); none → "no live session on E-NNNN".
- bare digits `N` → if a live session has `endless_session_id == N` **xor** a live
  session has `active_task_id == N`, use the unique match; if **both** match
  different sessions → ambiguous error telling the user to write `E-N` for the task
  (Mike confirmed: ambiguous → error).
- non-numeric → treat as a session ref: prefix-match `harness_session_id` (uuid),
  like `session cd`.
- session ref → that session's `pane_id` (its `sessions.process`).

### `session back`
1. Require tmux; resolve this client's stack.
2. Pop the top token:
   - `%pane` token → use directly; if the pane no longer exists, drop and pop next.
   - session-id token → resolve to that session's *current* live pane; if the
     session is no longer live, drop and pop next.
3. If the stack drains → **spawn-back fallback**: read this window's
   `@endless_spawned_by` (set at spawn = spawner's session id; `task_cmd.py`)
   and switch to that session's current live pane. Live re-resolution is a strict
   superset of seeding (handles a spawner restarting into a new pane) with zero
   change to the spawn path.
4. `tmux switch-client -t <pane>`.
5. Nothing left and no live spawner → message "no previous session".

## Files

- `src/endless/cli.py` (~line 880, in the `session` group) — register
  `@session_cmd.command("goto")` (one positional `target_ref`) and
  `@session_cmd.command("back")`, each delegating into `session_cmd.py`.
- `src/endless/session_cmd.py` — add `session_goto(target_ref)`, `session_back()`,
  and helpers:
  - `_resolve_goto_target(ref, live)` → `(target_pane, label)`.
  - `_backstack_key()` (client name → sanitized option suffix),
    `_backstack_read()/_write()/_push()/_pop()` (tmux option get/set).
  - `_tmux_switch_client(pane)`, `_pane_exists(pane)` (subprocess wrappers,
    alongside existing `_tmux_window_pane_ids`).
  - `_session_pane(live, session_id)` (session id → current live pane),
    `_spawner_pane(live)` (read `@endless_spawned_by` → live pane).
  - Reuse `_live_sessions`, `_project_root_from_cwd`-style resolution as `session
    cd` does.

## Tests — `tests/test_session_goto_back.py` (model: `tests/test_session_cd.py`)

Mock `_live_sessions` + `subprocess.run` (tmux), assert the exact tmux commands:
- goto by task id → pushes current session token, switches to the live session's pane.
- goto by session id / uuid prefix → switches to that pane.
- goto unknown / task with no live session → friendly error, no switch, nothing pushed.
- goto ambiguous bare number → error naming `E-N`, no switch.
- back pops the pushed token (session id → current pane) and switches.
- back empty stack but `@endless_spawned_by` set → switches to spawner's pane.
- back empty stack, no live spawner → "no previous session".
- back drops a stale token (dead pane / ended session) and pops the next.
- both verbs outside tmux → friendly error.

## Verification (end-to-end)
1. `just build` in the worktree (current candidate `bin/endless-go`).
2. `just test` — new suite green, no regressions.
3. Manual, inside tmux from the worktree (sandbox-routed): `goto` a live
   task/session → focus moves; `back` → returns; from a spawned session's pane,
   `back` with empty stack → returns to the spawner; `back` from a fresh pane →
   "no previous session".

## Out of scope (follow-up filed)
- Durable navigation trail (DB, captures manual moves via tmux hooks, queryable
  for usability analysis / finding lost sessions) — separate task, `--cleans-up E-1681`.
- The `session next` view itself (E-1465).
