Implements ED-1571, the one part of E-1944's outcome that was decided and never
filed.

Under ED-1567 a CANDIDATE binary may never migrate the real ledger. But
`_resolve_land_endless_go` (src/endless/worktree_cmd.py) hands a self_dev
land the WORKTREE's own binary, and E-1664 made that an invariant rather than a
choice: "the only binary whose embedded schema/enums match the just-written rows
is the worktree's own build — never the not-yet-refreshed global." That binary is
a candidate by `candidateBuild()`'s definition — its path carries the worktree
marker.

So the moment E-2020 lands, a self_dev land has no binary permitted to apply its
own migration: the installed one does not carry it, the worktree one is not
allowed to run it. That is why this exists, and it is why it blocks E-2020 rather
than following it.

Build a migration-only executable from the landing branch, carrying the
migration set and nothing else. It performs migration steps in FULL — DDL plus
the DML those migrations define: enum seed rows, backfills, the INSERT ... SELECT
of a table rebuild. What it excludes is application runtime: it never serves a
hook, never runs a task command, never touches business data outside a
migration. That exclusion is what makes it immune to the
binary-expects-a-schema failure, because it has no expectations beyond the
migrations it carries.

`worktree land` builds and invokes it at the existing apply step (E-1941's
ordering: after the ff-merge, before `_record_landing`) instead of calling
`endless db apply-change` with the worktree binary.

Scope is self_dev ONLY. Every other project has one installed binary and no land
at all, so it carries and applies its own migrations under ED-1570; no separate
executable exists there, and nothing in this task may assume one does.

Two things to settle while planning, not now:
- `_record_landing` still runs on the worktree binary for the same E-1664
  reason, against a ledger this executable just migrated. Whether that remains
  correct under ED-1570's exact-agreement rule needs an answer.
- E-1709 rebuilds the worktree binary before land uses it. If the migration
  executable replaces that usage, E-1709's rebuild may be serving only
  `_record_landing` afterward.

# Verification

`.endless/tasks/e-2088/`, run only through the runner — `just verify E-2088` or
`endless task verify E-2088`. Never executed directly: `_guard.sh` refuses that,
and a suite exercising land-time migration against your real `HOME` is precisely
the run that must not happen.

Shape: a `verify.toml` whose first `[[check]]` is a `gotest` runner over the
executable's unit tests — the fail-fast half — plus a `verify.sh` driving a land
end-to-end. The script sources `_harness.sh`, opens with the DO-NOT-EDIT header
naming E-2088, uses `section` / `assert_eq` / `assert_contains`, and calls
`summary` last; shipped fixtures are read from `$ENDLESS_VERIFY_DIR`.

The runner's temp `HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` are what make it safe to run a
real migration, so nothing here passes `--config-dir`.

1. The executable applies a migration end to end against a throwaway database:
   version before, version after, and the DML the migration defines actually ran
   (seed rows present, backfill applied), not just the DDL.
2. It refuses to do anything that is not a migration — assert the binary exposes
   no hook, task, or query surface, since "it never serves a hook" is the
   property that makes it immune to the binary-expects-a-schema failure and is
   otherwise untested.
3. `worktree land` invokes it at E-1941's apply step, between the ff-merge and
   `_record_landing`, and a failure there produces the existing post-merge
   message telling the operator to re-run rather than restore.
4. Landing a branch with no migration does not build or invoke it.
5. In a non-self_dev project no such executable exists and the installed binary
   applies its own migrations under ED-1570 — assert the self_dev-only scope
   rather than assuming it.
6. The worktree binary is still what `_record_landing` runs, against the ledger
   this executable just migrated. Assert that pairing works, because it is the
   half of E-1664 that survives E-2088 and nothing else covers it.

Coverage that must outlive the land is mirrored into the durable Go suite —
assertion 2's "no application surface" check in particular, since it is a
property of the build that would otherwise erode silently.

# Plan — Bracket an agent's CLI refusal with a repeated one-line verdict

## The failure this fixes, measured

`endless task update E-2093 --title <104 chars>` refuses with 17 lines on
stderr. The verdict is line 2:

    1
    2   Error: Title is 104 characters; max is 100.
    3
    4-16  (fourteen lines of guidance on how to shape a title)
    17

An agent piping `2>&1 | tail -3` keeps lines 15-17 — the tail of the guidance
block. The one line that names the constraint is the one line a small window
cannot see.

What that cost, in one session, across `task add` and `task update` (both call
`validate_title`, task_cmd.py, from :2252 and :4624):

1. `task add`, title 107 chars — refused. Read the fragment as a SHAPE
   complaint, reworded, and passed at 94 by accident while believing the shape
   was the problem.
2. `task add`, description 1032 > 1024 — refused.
3. `task update --title`, 141 chars — refused.
4. `task update --title`, 107 chars — refused. Thirty-four characters shaved
   between attempts 3 and 4 without ever reading the number the error stated
   both times. That is editing toward a constraint rather than reading it.
5. `--title "test"` written to a LIVE task to probe the validator — a mutation
   of real state to learn what the error had already said twice.
6. `--description-file` with newlines — refused.

Five refusals and one junk write, all against a message that was correct,
complete, and on stderr the whole time.

## The change

The bracket renders when EITHER an agent is running the command or a human
asked to see what one sees:

    agent_env.present() or agent_help.agent_view_requested()

Both, not one. An earlier draft of this plan said "NOT the `--agent-view` flag,
because an agent will never pass a flag it does not know it needs." The premise
is true and the conclusion is wrong: `--agent-view` is not a detection
mechanism, it is a HUMAN's override for previewing agent-facing output while
debugging. Excluding it would take that away, and the whole point of the flag is
to make output like this inspectable.

`agent_help._should_augment()` already composes exactly this predicate, for
exactly this reason — its docstring reads "An agent is reading this help, or a
human asked to see what one sees." Reuse or extract it; do NOT write a fourth
spelling of the question. That module's history is two consolidations of this
same duplication (E-1966 folded in a private `is_claude_code_agent()`, E-2006
folded in the last `!= UNKNOWN` comparison), and adding another would undo
them.

So refusals are emitted as:

    <verdict line>
    <blank>
    … today's guidance block, unchanged …
    <blank>
    <verdict line>          ← byte-identical to the first

The two lines are IDENTICAL, deliberately. Split them — verdict first, remedy
last — and `head -N` yields the problem without the fix while `tail -N` yields
the fix without the problem. Identical means whichever end survives is
sufficient alone, and seeing both reads as one repeat rather than two findings.

Length is unconstrained: `head`/`tail` are line-based, so a 200-character line
survives whole. Keep it to one dense line rather than a paragraph — a paragraph
invites the same skimming that caused this.

## What the verdict line must carry

Ordered by what would have stopped the failure above at attempt 3:

1. **Measured numbers, never an adjective.** `title 107>100 chars`, not "too
   long". The number is what makes the correction computable.
2. **A fixed sentinel plus the command and field**: `ENDLESS-ERROR task add:`.
   A bare error line read out of context does not say what produced it.
3. **Where the overflow goes**, not merely "shorten": `long-form goes in
   --analysis (rationale) or --text (plan); the title names WHAT`. Without
   this an agent mangles the field to fit instead of relocating the content —
   which is what happened.
4. **Whether anything changed**: `Nothing was created.` A refusal leaves an
   agent wondering whether it partially applied; that uncertainty is part of
   what produced the junk write in step 5.
5. **Every problem at once**, not the first. See below.

Deliberately NOT in it: the template, the HOW-vs-WHAT rationale, the examples.
Those are worth having and worth losing.

Not JSON, not key=value. A stable prefix and a plain sentence parses fine and
stays readable when a human hits it.

Worked example, ~170 characters:

    ENDLESS-ERROR task add: title 107>100 chars; description 1032>1024 chars. Long-form goes in --analysis (rationale) or --text (plan); the title names WHAT. Nothing was created.

## Collect every problem before refusing

Today `validate_title` raises on the first failure, so the sequence is: fix the
title, resubmit, discover the description. Steps 1-2 and 3-6 above are both
that shape. The validators for title, description and analysis on `task add`
and `task update` should accumulate their findings and refuse once, with all of
them in the verdict line.

Scope this to those validators on those two verbs. It is not a project-wide
refactor of every ClickException.

## Shape it as a shared helper

A rule that reaches two messages is not a convention. Add one helper — e.g.
`agent_error(summary: str, guidance: str)` beside the existing agent-facing
machinery — that renders the bracketed form when `agent_env.present()` and
today's plain form otherwise. Adopt it first in the title/description
validators, and document it so a new refusal reaches for it.

## Humans see no change

The duplication is agent-only. A person reading the full message in a terminal
gets today's output byte for byte. This is a requirement, not a nicety: a
repeated long line is noise to a reader who was never going to truncate it.

## Boundaries

- Does NOT touch which stream errors go to. They are already on stderr, already
  complete; the agent truncated them. Nothing about stdout/stderr changes.
- Does NOT add a PreToolUse matcher against `2>&1 | tail`. That was considered
  and rejected: it targets a correlate, would not catch `| tail -N` over a long
  stdout report, and would fire on `go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -30`, which is
  correct usage (a failing `go test` writes to stdout; a failing `endless`
  leaves stdout empty — measured).
- Does NOT reorder the existing guidance. The bracket makes order irrelevant.

## PRODUCT

Nothing here is Endless-specific. Every project using Endless is driven by
agents that pipe and truncate CLI output, and every CLI puts its verdict first
and its teaching after. The agent-gated bracket belongs in the shipped CLI, and
the detection signal (`agent_env.present()`) already ships.

## Verify — .endless/tasks/e-<id>/verify.sh

1. Fail-fast unit gate: the Python tests this task adds.
2. Under a simulated agent env, a refusal's first and last lines are
   byte-identical.
3. That line carries the measured numbers, the command, the field, the
   destination for long-form content, and the no-change statement.
4. `… 2>&1 | tail -3` and `… 2>&1 | head -3` of the same refusal EACH contain
   the verdict — the two ends of the property.
5. With no agent env AND no --agent-view, the message is byte-identical to
   today's: no duplication, no sentinel.
6. With no agent env but --agent-view passed, the bracket IS rendered — the
   flag's purpose is to let a human see what an agent sees, so a version that
   only fires on detection would make agent-facing output the one thing
   --agent-view cannot show.
7. A call that violates title AND description limits at once names both in one
   verdict line and refuses once.
8. A refused call mutated nothing.

So a resumed pane lacks the window identity that _current_pane_task() (the E-1968 clobber guard, session_cmd.py) and session-status focal resolution read from @endless_task_id. fields.text:
# Make `session resume` re-bind the tmux window options on the current pane

## Problem
`resume_session` (src/endless/session_cmd.py) resolves the target, then
`os.chdir(worktree)` + `os.execvp("claude", ["claude","--resume",uuid])`
(session_cmd.py). It sets NO tmux window options. So a pane resumed into
lacks the `@endless_*` window identity that a spawned window carries.

The four options and who sets them today:
- `@endless_task_id`, `@endless_project_id`, `@endless_spawned_by` — written ONLY
  by the spawn launcher (internal/spawnlaunchcmd/spawn_launch.go ->
  tmux_driver.go). Never on the resume path.
- `@endless_session_uuid` — written by the hook every event
  (internal/hookcmd/claude.go, setTmuxSessionUUID), meant to self-heal.

## Why it matters
A resumed pane with no `@endless_task_id` silently loses:
- `_current_pane_task()` — the E-1968 clobber guard in resume itself
  (session_cmd.py) can't see the pane's held task.
- `session status` focal-task resolution, which reads the window's
  `@endless_task_id`.

## Fix
On the resume path, before `os.execvp`, set the window options on the current
pane to match a spawned window:
- `@endless_task_id` = resolved task id
- `@endless_project_id` = resolved project id
- `@endless_session_uuid` = resolved session uuid (set it here rather than
  depend on the hook's per-event self-heal, which is more fragile — see below)

Open design question for the implementer: `@endless_spawned_by` means "which
session spawned this window." A resumed pane was NOT spawned by `task spawn`, so
setting it is debatable — likely omit it (or record a resume-origin marker).
Decide during implementation; task_id/project_id/session_uuid are the clear wins.

## Not a regression
Verified via git pickaxe: `git log -S 'set -w' -- src/endless/session_cmd.py`
and `-S '@endless_task_id' -- …` both return zero commits. resume has been
option-less since it was introduced (eb2206ad). None of E-2074/E-2102/E-1918/
E-1851/E-1898/E-1976 touched the resume/hook option writes. This is a
long-standing design gap, not a recent breakage.

## Related but SEPARATE (do not fold in)
A distinct symptom was observed alongside this: `@endless_session_uuid` absent
even though the hook should self-heal it every event. That points at the hook
not reaching claude.go for the affected session (candidates: the
`shouldSkipForWorktree` early return at claude.go, or a stale/missing
worktree-local hook wiring in that worktree's .claude/settings.json). That is a
hook-firing/wiring diagnostic, not confirmed as a code defect, and is NOT part
of this task. Setting session_uuid on the resume path (above) makes resume
robust to it regardless.

## Origin
Found while debugging a `session resume` in an unrelated session's worktree; the
task that session happened to be under (E-1834) is NOT related to this bug.

fields.analysis:
## What the column says today

`session status` renders one column between the task-type letter and the task
id (`unsettledMark`, internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go, rendered
at :679). Two states: ◆ when the row's worktree is unsettled, blank otherwise.

## What it says after this change

Three states. The column answers "is there work product here, and where is
it?":

| Glyph | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| ◆ | work product, still outstanding | anything unsettled |
| ⊙ | **no work product yet** | never spawned (no worktree), **or** `underway` with a settled worktree |
| blank | work product, all of it landed | `unverified` + settled |

The two cases sharing ⊙ are deliberate and are the point of the task: a task
nobody has picked up and a task a session is sitting on that has produced
nothing are the same fact about the work. The reader does not need this column
to tell those apart — the action icon and the status already do — so it must
not try to.

## The rule, decided

**⊙ when the row's task status is `underway` or earlier and the worktree is not
unsettled.** Blank when the status is past `underway` (`unverified`,
`unreviewed`, `confirmed`, `assumed`, `completed`) and the worktree is not
unsettled. ◆ whenever the worktree is unsettled, unchanged and taking
precedence over both.

Status is the discriminator, not landing history. `task_landings` is not a
reliable record of what reached main — E-2087 measured branches whose content
is demonstrably on main with no landing row at all — and a git-side answer
(`git log <base> --grep "E-<id>:"`) would put a new probe on a per-row hot
path. Status is already on `SessionStatusRow`, costs nothing, and reproduces
every case above.

Its one known mis-signal, accepted: a task that lands mid-flight and keeps
working is `underway` with real landed work and wears ⊙. It is still true that
nothing is outstanding. Label the glyph in the legend by what it MEANS, not by
what it is derived from, so the derivation can be sharpened later without the
vocabulary changing.

## The glyph, decided

**⊙ (U+2299 CIRCLED DOT OPERATOR).**

- It shares the unsettledMark column with only ◆ and blank, so the sole
  within-column distinction is circle vs diamond — different silhouettes, which
  ◇ (U+25C7) would not have given.
- The other circled-operator glyphs — ⊗ blocked, ⏸ blocks, ⊘ hidden, ⊕ queued —
  live in `blockField`/`hiddenField`/`relationField`, rendered after the id and
  phase char (:679-682). Position disambiguates them from this column.
- Width: U+2299 is East Asian Ambiguous, the same class as the already-shipped
  ⊘. Add a width assertion beside `TestHiddenGlyphWidth` rather than assuming.
- Known co-occurrence, accepted: an untriaged row carries ◌ (`actTriage`) in
  column 1 and will usually also carry ⊙ here, so `◌ T⊙E-2107` puts two round
  glyphs on one line. They mean compatible things and sit in different columns.

## Constraints the column imposes

- Display width 1. The prefix is a fixed 13 columns and the alignment
  guarantee ⏚/⁇/◆ carry (E-1765) holds only if every state in the slot matches.
- `buildLegend` shows a decoration only when a row bears it; ⊙ follows that
  rule and is labelled there — suggested label: "not started".
- ◆ vetoes dimming (E-1707) because it means "still something to do". ⊙ means
  the opposite and must NOT veto dimming — a never-started `later` row should
  still read dim.
- The "no worktree" half of the signal is already computed:
  `monitor.UnsettledDetail.HasWorktree`. `SessionStatusRow` carries `Unsettled`
  today and needs the second flag filled by the same
  `AnnotateSessionStatusUnsettled` pass.

## Scope

Implements ED-1587. Three pieces, in order:

1. **Construction.** `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py` and `:1653` build
   `f"task/{task_id}-{slug}"`. Both become `f"task/{task_id}"`. Whatever
   computes the slug for this purpose goes with them if nothing else uses it.

2. **Migration of the ~139 existing branches.** They are local-only — no
   remote, no PRs, no CI — so `git branch -m task/<id>-<slug> task/<id>` is
   cheap and safe. Each has a live worktree checked out on it, so the rename
   must go through git (which updates the worktree's HEAD), never by editing
   refs. Decide and state whether this is a one-shot `db apply-change`-style
   step or a resolver that accepts both forms during a transition; a one-shot
   rename is simpler and this project has no other clones to coordinate with.
   Sessions are live in some of these worktrees, so the rename must not run
   under them unannounced — gate it the way the reaper gates on
   `WorktreeInUse`, or require it to be run deliberately.

3. **Retire `task_landings.branch`.** Once the name is derivable the column is
   redundant. Two consequences worth doing in the same pass, because they are
   the reason the decision was made:
   - E-1719's record-only landing recorded no branch, which is why
     `maybeReapWorktree` scans it as `sql.NullString`. That case disappears.
   - E-2087 added a git fallback (`git symbolic-ref --short HEAD`) so a
     worktree with no landing row could still have its branch deleted at reap
     time, plus a carve-out that deliberately does NOT apply the fallback to a
     NULL-branch landing row. Both go away: the reaper derives `task/<id>`
     from the task id it already has.

   The column also feeds `internal/monitor/session_notices.go` and the
   `task landed` surface; check every reader before dropping it, and prefer
   deriving over reading rather than leaving a second source of truth.

## Also update

- `ED-1167` — supersede it via `endless decision supersede`, not by editing it.
- The guide's worktree/branch prose, wherever it shows a slug branch name.
- Any test fixture that hardcodes a `task/<id>-<slug>` branch.

## Out of scope

A configurable branch pattern. ED-1587 rejects it explicitly and says why.

fields.text: The gate lives in cli.py and needs work.

# E-787: Add `outcome` field and `task decline` verb

## Context

Endless tasks have terminal statuses (`confirmed`, `assumed`, `declined`, `obsolete`) but no field for capturing **why** a task ended that way. Today the answer lives in commit messages, chat transcripts, or nowhere at all — searchable retrieval is impossible. E-787 adds an `outcome TEXT` column, a `task decline` verb that requires a reason, and `--outcome` flags on the other terminal-status entry points.

The asymmetry — `--reason` is required on `decline` but `--outcome` is optional on `confirm`/`assume`/`replace` — is intentional. Confirming a task usually means "we tested it and it worked" (not informative to log). Declining a task is uncommon and the reason is rarely obvious without explanation; forcing capture exactly there is where the cost/value math lands.

E-787 was previously marked `declined` in error (the `declined` enum value half had shipped, the rest hadn't). Status is now `ready`, work resumes here.

### Decisions already locked with Mike

1. `--reason` on `task decline`, `--outcome` everywhere else. Both write to the same `outcome` column. Pave the cowpath: each verb gets the flag name agents instinctively type for it.
2. Outcome is REQUIRED whenever the resulting status is `declined`, regardless of entry point (`task decline`, `task update --status declined`, `task replace --status declined`). No back doors.
3. `task replace` gains optional `--status <s>` (default `obsolete`) and `--outcome <text>`.
4. `task update --outcome` works standalone or alongside `--status`. Emits an event like every other field update — that's the whole point of the architecture (this was the E-993 lesson).
5. Outcome is mutable via `task update --outcome` (event-sourced, not a frozen field).

### Decisions made by me, flagged here for review

6. **Event shape: extend `task.status_changed` with optional `Outcome`.** *(Revised during Phase 2 implementation. Original Decision #6 had this backwards — see below.)* All dedicated terminal-status verbs (`task decline`, `task confirm`, `task assume`) emit `task.status_changed` with an optional `outcome` field on the payload. The cascade semantics already built into `task.status_changed` are preserved; outcome applies to the root task only (per Decision #8). `update_plan` continues to use `task.fields_updated` for multi-field updates (which can include status); `replace_task` routes its status+outcome write through `update_plan`, so its output is `task.fields_updated`. **Original framing was wrong:** I'd planned to switch `complete_item`/`assume_item` from `task.status_changed` to `task.fields_updated`, but `task.fields_updated` has no cascade support — switching would have silently broken cascade. Extending `task.status_changed` keeps that purpose-built event focused on its purpose and adds outcome with minimal surface area (one struct field, two ~5-line write paths in executor.go and projector.go).

7. **`replace_task` event-emission fix is in scope.** Currently `replace_task` (task_cmd.py) does raw SQL — both the `task_deps` insert and the `UPDATE tasks SET status='obsolete'`. This violates the events-authoritative invariant we just reaffirmed in E-993. Adding `--outcome`/`--status` to it is impossible without going through events, so the status-write half MUST be fixed here. The `task_deps` insert (also raw SQL) is the same bug shape but lives in E-957's typed-link territory; I'm leaving it alone in this plan and will note it as a follow-up.

8. **Cascade + outcome:** when `task confirm --cascade --outcome "x"` is used, the outcome applies to the root task only. Descendants get cascaded confirm with no outcome. Matches existing cascade UX (only the root gets explicit attention).

9. **`task show --outcome` flag honors spec literally.** In default human mode, outcome renders only when `--outcome` is passed. In `--llm` and `--json` modes, outcome always renders when set (those modes already include all fields). Worth revisiting later — a one-line outcome on a terminal task is short enough to always display by default — but defer that to a follow-up.

10. **Validation enforced at the task_cmd impl layer**, not the CLI. `decline_item`, `update_plan`, `replace_task` each call a shared `_require_outcome_for_declined(status, outcome)` helper. Centralizes the rule so all entry points behave identically.

---

## Prerequisites

**E-1020 (precursor, blocking): Add `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` support to Python CLI.**

Currently `src/endless/config.py` hardcodes `Path.home() / ".config" / "endless"`. The Go side (`internal/monitor/db.go`) honors `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`; Python doesn't. This parity gap blocks isolated binary-level testing of Python CLI commands — without it, Phase 5 of E-787 cannot run against a copied DB and would silently mutate `~/.config/endless/endless.db`.

Scope of precursor:
- `src/endless/config.py`: read `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` env var first, fall back to `Path.home() / ".config"`. Mirror the Go-side logic in `internal/monitor/db.go:ConfigDir()`.
- Audit other `Path.home()` references in `src/endless/` to ensure all config-relative paths derive from `CONFIG_DIR` rather than re-deriving from `Path.home()`.
- pytest should still pass (the `isolated_env` fixture overrides `CONFIG_DIR` directly via monkeypatch, bypassing the env-var read path entirely).
- Manual verification: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/cfg-test ./bin/endless task list` should not touch `~/.config/endless/endless.db`.

Estimated size: ~30 lines. E-787 is now formally `blocked_by E-1020`. Also serves as concrete input to E-995's design — it's exactly the kind of isolation primitive E-995 will need to formalize.

### Decisions recorded (linked to E-787)

- E-1021 — Use `--reason` on `task decline` and `--outcome` elsewhere
- E-1022 — Require outcome at every entry point that lands a task in declined
- E-1023 — Use `task.fields_updated` for terminal-status writes; deprecate `task.status_changed` for new code
- E-1024 — Include `replace_task` event-emission fix in E-787 scope
- E-1025 — Apply cascade outcome to root task only, not descendants
- E-1026 — Enforce outcome validation at task_cmd impl layer, not CLI

---

## Implementation

### Phase 1 — Schema + Go projection/executor (must precede any event emission)

**`internal/schema/schema.sql`** (canonical, `//go:embed`-ed)
- Tasks table (lines 74-93): add `outcome TEXT` column. Place after `tier INTEGER` for diff readability.

**`src/endless/db.py`** (note: `_migrate_v5` was taken by E-957's task_deps active-voice migration since planning; using `_migrate_v6`)
- After `_migrate_v5` (the task_deps active-voice migration), add `_migrate_v6(conn)`:
  ```python
  def _migrate_v6(conn: sqlite3.Connection):
      """Schema v6: add outcome column to tasks (E-787)."""
      if _has_table(conn, "tasks") and not _has_column(conn, "tasks", "outcome"):
          conn.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN outcome TEXT")
          conn.commit()
  ```
- Wire into `_migrate()` orchestrator: add `_migrate_v6(conn)` after `_migrate_v5(conn)`.

**`internal/events/executor.go:258-262`** — `allowedFields` map: add `"outcome": "outcome"`.

**`internal/events/projector.go:225-229`** — `allowedFields` map: add `"outcome": "outcome"`.

**Critical:** executor REJECTS unknown fields (line 267), projector silently SKIPS them (line 234). Both maps must be updated *before* any event with `outcome` is emitted — otherwise live emit fails.

**`internal/web/data/types.go:68-84`** — add `Outcome string` to `TaskView` struct so the web UI can display it (web rendering itself is not in this plan; just the field availability).

**`internal/events/payload.go`** — `TaskFieldsUpdatedPayload` already supports arbitrary fields via `map[string]any`, no change needed. `TaskStatusChangedPayload` is unchanged (we're not extending it; new code uses `task.fields_updated`).

### Phase 2 — Python task_cmd implementations

**`src/endless/task_cmd.py`**

- New helper near top of the terminal-status section:
  ```python
  def _require_outcome_for_declined(status: str | None, outcome: str | None):
      if status == "declined" and not (outcome and outcome.strip()):
          raise click.ClickException(
              "An outcome is required when declining a task. "
              "Use --reason (on `task decline`) or --outcome to explain why."
          )
  ```

- New `decline_item(item_id: int, reason: str)`:
  - Validates reason is non-empty (handled at click layer too via `required=True`).
  - Emits ONE `task.fields_updated` with `{"status": "declined", "outcome": reason}`.
  - Mirrors structure of `complete_item` for output (cyan bullet, task title display).

- `complete_item` (lines 1314-1365):
  - Add `outcome: str | None = None` param.
  - Switch from `task.status_changed` to `task.fields_updated` with `{"status": "confirmed", **({"outcome": outcome} if outcome else {})}`.
  - Cascade: outcome applies only to root; descendants are cascaded via existing logic without outcome.

- `assume_item` (lines 1368-1419): same shape as `complete_item` change.

- `update_plan` (lines 1452-1551):
  - Add `outcome: str | None = None` param.
  - Add to fields-building block (around line 1538):
    ```python
    if outcome is not None:
        fields["outcome"] = outcome
        changed_names.append("outcome")
    ```
  - After all fields built, BEFORE emit_event, call `_require_outcome_for_declined(fields.get("status"), fields.get("outcome"))`. Note: `fields.get("outcome")` may be the existing DB value's stand-in if the user didn't pass `--outcome`; the rule only fires when user is *setting* status to declined without supplying outcome in this call.
  - Tier-1 auto-advance logic (line 1534) is unrelated; preserve.

- `replace_task` (lines 2146-2179) — fix to be event-sourced:
  - Add `status: str = "obsolete"` and `outcome: str | None = None` params.
  - Validate via `_require_outcome_for_declined(status, outcome)`.
  - Replace the `db.execute("UPDATE tasks SET status = 'obsolete', tier = 0 ...")` (lines 2171-2174) with a call to `update_plan(old_id, status=status, outcome=outcome)`. This routes the status/outcome write through `task.fields_updated` and the existing terminal-status tier-zero logic in the projector handles the `tier=0` automatically (projector.go already does this).
  - The `task_deps` INSERT (lines 2158-2162) stays as raw SQL for now. It's a separate event-sourcing gap living in E-957's typed-link territory; flagging as a follow-up rather than expanding scope here.
  - Output message stays.

- `detail_item` (`task show` rendering, around lines 1570-1720):
  - Add `show_outcome: bool = False` param.
  - Modify the SELECT in this function (around line 1580-1584) to include `outcome` column.
  - JSON mode (lines 1593-1623): always include `outcome` when set.
  - LLM mode (lines 1626-1663): always echo `outcome=<value>` when set, after `status` line.
  - Human-readable (lines 1665-1720+): only show outcome if `show_outcome` is True OR if it's set and the task is in a declined status (we owe the user the "why" for declines specifically). Worth confirming with Mike but I'm planning the latter; if pushback, drop to `show_outcome only`.

### Phase 3 — CLI wiring

**`src/endless/cli.py`**

- Status enum at lines 28-29 and 544-545: no change (`declined` and `obsolete` already present).

- `task update` (lines 560-589): add `@click.option("--outcome", default=None, help="Outcome / reason for status (required if status=declined)")`. Pass through to `update_plan`.

- `task confirm` (lines 618-626): add `@click.option("--outcome", default=None, help="Outcome — what was confirmed")`. Pass to `complete_item`.

- `task assume` (lines 629-637): add `@click.option("--outcome", default=None, help="Outcome — what was assumed")`. Pass to `assume_item`.

- New `task decline` command, after `task assume`:
  ```python
  @task_cmd.command("decline")
  @click.argument("item_ids", type=TASK_ID, nargs=-1, required=True)
  @click.option("--reason", required=True, help="Why this task is being declined")
  def task_decline(item_ids, reason):
      """Decline one or more tasks (sets status=declined; reason required)."""
      from endless.task_cmd import decline_item
      for item_id in item_ids:
          decline_item(item_id, reason=reason)
  ```

- `task replace` (lines ~706-713): add `--status` (default `"obsolete"`, choices match terminal statuses) and `--outcome`. Pass both to `replace_task`.

- `task show` (lines 397-418): add `@click.option("--outcome", "show_outcome", is_flag=True, help="Show outcome field")`. Pass to `detail_item`.

### Phase 4 — Tests

**`tests/test_cli.py`** — new test functions following the existing `CliRunner` + `isolated_env` fixture pattern (conftest.py):

1. `test_task_decline_writes_outcome` — decline E-X with `--reason "x"`, assert status=declined and outcome="x" in DB.
2. `test_task_decline_requires_reason` — invoke without `--reason`, assert click error.
3. `test_task_confirm_with_outcome` — confirm + `--outcome`, assert outcome stored.
4. `test_task_confirm_without_outcome_still_works` — outcome remains NULL, status=confirmed.
5. `test_task_assume_with_outcome` — same shape as #3.
6. `test_task_replace_default_obsolete` — `task replace E-X --by E-Y`, assert E-X status=obsolete.
7. `test_task_replace_with_status_declined_requires_outcome` — `task replace E-X --by E-Y --status declined` (no outcome) — error.
8. `test_task_replace_with_status_declined_and_outcome` — same with `--outcome` — succeeds, status=declined, outcome set.
9. `test_task_update_status_declined_requires_outcome` — `task update E-X --status declined` (no outcome) — error.
10. `test_task_update_outcome_standalone` — `task update E-X --outcome "x"` — succeeds, outcome updated, status untouched.
11. `test_task_show_outcome_flag` — `task show E-X --outcome` displays outcome.
12. `test_task_show_llm_mode_includes_outcome_when_set` — `task show E-X --llm` always includes outcome line when set.
13. `test_event_log_records_outcome` — after decline, read the JSONL event log and assert the `task.fields_updated` event contains both `status: "declined"` and `outcome: "<reason>"`.
14. `test_rebuild_db_preserves_outcome` — set outcome, run `endless rebuild-db`, assert outcome survives.

   **Note:** test #14 invokes a Go subprocess (`endless rebuild-db`), and the in-process `monkeypatch.setattr` does NOT propagate to subprocesses. The test must explicitly set `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (pointing to the pytest tmp_path's parent) in the `subprocess.run()` env before invoking the binary. This is contingent on Phase 4.5 confirming the Go side honors XDG; do not write this test until then.

### Phase 4.5 — Verify Go binaries respect isolation (spike, BEFORE writing test #14)

Read `cmd/endless-event/main.go` (`runRebuildDB`) and any other Go entry points that touch the DB. Confirm:

1. DB path comes from `monitor.DBPath()` (which reads `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`), not a hardcoded `~/.config/endless/`.
2. The temp/scratch DB used by `ProjectToTempDB` is derived from the configured root, not from `/tmp` with a fixed name that could collide between concurrent test runs.
3. No fallthrough hardcoded paths anywhere in the rebuild/validate/projection code paths.

If any of these fail, fix them BEFORE writing test #14 — without this verification, a test that subprocess-invokes `endless rebuild-db` could mutate `~/.config/endless/endless.db` despite the pytest fixture's monkeypatching.

This spike also serves as final confirmation that the precursor task (Python XDG support) was complete: invoke `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/spike ./bin/endless task list` against an empty config dir and confirm it does NOT touch the production DB.

### Phase 5 — Manual sanity verification against an isolated DB copy

**Prerequisites:**
- Precursor task complete (XDG support in Python CLI).

# Plan: Enforce Task and Decision Recording via Hooks

## Context

Per `docs/TASK_RECORDING_PROMPT.md`, Claude Code sessions on Endless repeatedly fail to record tasks before code changes and fail to record decisions when they emerge from discussion. Text-only reminders (CLAUDE.md, memory, session guide) are demonstrably insufficient: Claude knows the rule but does not consistently follow it.

Exploration revealed the enforcement substrate is more complete than the prompt suggested:

- A `PreToolUse` hook in `cmd/endless-hook/claude.go` already blocks `Write`/`Edit`/`NotebookEdit` when no working session exists, *if* the project's tracking mode is `enforce`.
- Endless defaults to `enforce` for registered projects (`internal/monitor/session.go`); `.endless/config.json` does not currently override it.
- `endless task start <id>` invokes `monitor.StartWorkSession()` and writes `active_task_id` per `session_id` to the `sessions` table.

Three real gaps remain, in order of impact:

1. **Task drift is the dominant cause of unrecorded changes.** PreToolUse only checks "is there *any* active task." Once Claude starts task A, every subsequent edit passes, even if Claude has switched focus to unrelated work. This is the workflow Endless was built to track (constantly switching focus without losing prior context), so detecting drift at the edit boundary is first-class.
2. **Decisions are invisible to PreToolUse.** Decisions emerge from chat and do not trigger Edit/Write, so the existing block has nothing to fire on. There is no enforcement mechanism for `--type decision` tasks today.
3. **No post-session verification.** The `SessionEnd` handler at `cmd/endless-hook/claude.go` only parses the transcript and ends the session. Edits attributed to no task slip through silently.

The intended outcome is defense in depth: PreToolUse catches drift in real time, Stop catches decisions, SessionEnd catches anything that slipped through both.

## Design Notes

**Calibration as a first-class feature.** Each enforcement check is intentionally strict and asks Claude (in the same prompt) to optionally include a banner suggesting how the rule could be relaxed. Suggestions are persisted to a `suggestions` table and surface inline in the chat (visible to Mike at the moment they happen) plus as a count at next SessionStart. No suggestion auto-applies; Mike is the only one who can turn a suggestion into a code or config change. This makes the system get smarter from real-world use rather than from upfront guesses, and it ensures Claude cannot weaken its own enforcement.

**No dismiss action on suggestions.** AI output is non-deterministic, so reliably comparing a fresh suggestion against prior dismissals would require an AI call per hook (too expensive). Suggestions accumulate as a backlog; Mike accepts the worthwhile ones and leaves the rest. If accumulation becomes unwieldy, a `mute` action can be added later.

**Why ask Claude instead of doing forensics.** The hook already sees every Edit/Write through PostToolUse. We have an authoritative edit log natively, no `git diff` needed. And Claude knows what work it just did, so prompting Claude to attribute edits in real time beats post-hoc reconstruction.

## Recommended Approach

Three layers, each independently shippable. Together they form one tight mechanism around the per-task edit-set.

### Layer A: Per-Task Edit-Set and Drift Detection (PreToolUse)

**Goal**: every Edit/Write fires against an explicit, narrow active task. New files outside the task's scope force Claude to switch tasks, create a sub-task, or extend scope before the edit lands.

**New concept**: a per-task edit-set. New table `task_files` (`task_id`, `file_path`, `first_edited_at`, `first_edited_session_id`). Populated by PostToolUse on first edit of a file within an active task; subsequent edits to the same file are no-ops on the table.

**PreToolUse logic** (extends `cmd/endless-hook/claude.go`):

1. Existing block: no active session → block as today.
2. Active session exists → resolve target file path from `payload.ToolInput`.
3. Pass if any of: file is in `task_files` for the active task, file path appears in the active task's `tasks.text`, or file path appears in the linked plan file (`sessions.plan_file_path` or task-attached plan).
4. Otherwise block (`exit 2` + stderr) with this message:

   > Editing `<path>` but it is not in scope of active task E-Y "<title>". Choose:
   >
   > - `endless task start <id>` to switch focus (active task is preserved)
   > - `endless task add "<short title>" --parent E-Y` for a sub-task
   > - `endless task touch E-Y --add-file <path>` if `<path>` is genuinely part of E-Y's scope
   >
   > If you believe this prompt is wrong here, also include a banner in your next response:
   >
   > `**SUGGESTION (drift_detection):** <one-line explanation of why this should not have blocked>`

The post-hook (UserPromptSubmit of the next turn) parses the prior assistant turn for the banner and writes any captured suggestion to the `suggestions` table.

**Strict scope check by design**: file membership requires literal appearance in `task_files`, `tasks.text`, or the linked plan file. Loose heuristics (directory-prefix match, language-of-file match) are deliberately not in v1; they emerge from the suggestions log if the data warrants.

**Files to modify**:
- `cmd/endless-hook/claude.go` (extend `handlePreToolUse`)
- `cmd/endless-hook/claude.go` (extend `handlePostToolUseSession` to record `task_files` entries)
- `cmd/endless-hook/claude.go` (extend `UserPromptSubmit` to parse banners from prior assistant turn)
- `internal/monitor/files.go` (new): `RegisterTaskFile(taskID, sessionID, filePath)`, `IsFileInTaskScope(taskID, filePath) bool`
- `internal/monitor/suggestions.go` (new): `RecordSuggestion(sessionID, source, triggerCtx, suggestion) error`
- `sql/schema.sql` and a migration for `task_files` and `suggestions`

### Layer B: Decision Checkpoint on Stop (always-ask)

**Goal**: every Stop forces Claude to explicitly confirm presence/absence of decisions, removing the silent-skip failure mode.

**Mechanism**: extend the `Stop` case in `cmd/endless-hook/claude.go`. After `ParseTranscript` and `IdleSession`, return a `Stop` hook response with `decision: "block"` and reason:

> Before stopping, confirm: were any architectural decisions made or refined this turn? If yes, record them with `endless task add --type decision "..."`. If no, reply with `**NO DECISIONS THIS TURN**`.
>
> If you believe this prompt is wrong for this turn pattern, also include:
>
> `**SUGGESTION (decision_checkpoint):** <one-line explanation>`

The post-hook on next UserPromptSubmit parses the prior assistant turn for either the no-decisions confirmation, a recorded decision-task creation, or a suggestion banner. Suggestions land in `suggestions`; non-compliance is recorded but does not re-block (the user has moved on).

**No regex-based decision detection.** Earlier drafts proposed scanning the transcript for phrases like "let's go with." Decisions are semantic, not lexical, and the proxy-by-shape approach fails on the common pattern (user asks → Claude proposes options → user picks → Claude implements). Always-ask is cheaper and more robust.

**Files to modify**:
- `cmd/endless-hook/claude.go` (Stop case)
- `cmd/endless-hook/claude.go` (UserPromptSubmit, banner parsing shared with Layer A)

### Layer C: SessionEnd Manifest Backstop

**Goal**: catch any edit that slipped past Layers A and B, surface for retroactive recording at the next session.

**Mechanism**: extend the `SessionEnd` case in `cmd/endless-hook/claude.go`. The `task_files` table from Layer A already records every edit-time `(task_id, session_id, file_path)`. SessionEnd queries for files this session edited that have no `task_id` association (this should be empty in steady state once Layer A is in place; this is a backstop). If any are found, write a row to a new `pending_audits` table (`session_id`, `project_id`, `files`, `created_at`, `cleared_at NULL`).

At next `SessionStart` (`cmd/endless-hook/claude.go`), check `pending_audits WHERE cleared_at IS NULL`. If any exist, inject as `additional_context`:

> Previous session ended with `<N>` unattributed edit(s): `<file list>`. Before continuing, create tasks for these or run `endless audit clear <id>` if they should not be tasked.

**Files to modify**:
- `cmd/endless-hook/claude.go` (SessionEnd case)
- `cmd/endless-hook/claude.go` (SessionStart, surface pending audits)
- `cmd/endless/audit_cmd.go` (new): `endless audit list`, `endless audit clear <id>`
- Schema: add `pending_audits` table

## Suggestions Capture (cross-cutting, used by all layers)

### Schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE suggestions (
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  session_id  TEXT NOT NULL,
  source      TEXT NOT NULL,           -- 'drift_detection' | 'decision_checkpoint' | future
  trigger_ctx TEXT,                    -- file path, turn excerpt, audit summary
  suggestion  TEXT NOT NULL,           -- Claude's banner text
  created_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
  task_id     INTEGER,                 -- NULL=open, set=accepted into a task
  notes       TEXT,
  FOREIGN KEY (task_id) REFERENCES tasks(id)
);
```

`task_id IS NULL` is the open-suggestion state; `task_id` populated means the suggestion has been accepted and the resulting task lives at `tasks.id = task_id`.

### Banner format (in Claude's response)

```
**SUGGESTION (<source>):** <one-line description of the rule relaxation Claude proposes>
```

The post-hook on next UserPromptSubmit (or Stop, whichever fires first) parses the prior assistant turn for this banner using a fixed regex (the banner format is structured, not the suggestion content). One row per banner.

### CLI

- `endless suggestions list [--source drift_detection|decision_checkpoint] [--all]` — defaults to open suggestions (task_id IS NULL).
- `endless suggestions show <id>`
- `endless suggestions accept <id> [--type chore] [--parent <task-id>]` — runs `endless task add` with the suggestion text as the task body, then sets `suggestions.task_id`. Default type is `chore`.

### Surfacing to Mike

1. **Inline at moment of capture**: Claude's response itself contains the banner, displayed in your terminal naturally. No separate notification needed for in-session visibility.
2. **SessionStart context**: if `count(suggestions WHERE task_id IS NULL) > 0`, inject a one-line reminder. Quiet when none exist.
3. **Tmux alert**: piggy-back on the existing `claude-tmux-alert` global hook (already wired in `~/.claude/settings.json`). When a suggestion lands, fire the alert so the tmux indicator changes.

## Config Knobs (for development friction control)

`.endless/config.json` gains a `checks` map:

```json
{
  "tracking": "enforce",
  "checks": {
    "task_required":       true,
    "drift_detection":     true,
    "decision_checkpoint": true,
    "session_audit":       true

}
```

Each check reads its own flag; defaults to `true` when absent. Disabling one disables only that check, not the broader hook system.

CLI for fast toggling without hand-editing JSON in the heat of debugging:


# Plan: Refactor Endless Config Loading onto go-cfgstore

## Context

While testing E-917 (drift detection), Mike set `"checks": {"drift_detection": true}` in `~/.config/endless/config.json` (the global config). The check defaulted to OFF and the feature appeared dead because my code in `internal/monitor/checks.go` reads only `<project>/.endless/config.json` (per-project). Time was wasted debugging a layering mismatch the codebase should never have allowed.

The deeper problem: I copied the existing precedent set by `monitor.GetTrackingMode` at `internal/monitor/session.go`. Both functions reimplement config layering ad hoc with raw `os.ReadFile` + `json.Unmarshal`, ignoring Mike's house package `go-cfgstore` which exists for exactly this purpose, plus `go-doterr` for errors and `go-dt` for paths. So this task replaces *both* bespoke readers, not just the new one.

The proximate win: setting any check or tracking value in either layer works with predictable precedence. The structural win: Endless config moves onto house standards, future config additions follow one pattern, and the merge semantics for every field are explicitly documented instead of accidentally inferred from whichever reader you happen to be looking at.

## Scope

**In scope:**
- New `internal/config/` package using `go-cfgstore`, `go-doterr`, `go-dt`.
- Refactor `monitor.GetTrackingMode` and `monitor.IsCheckEnabled` to use it.
- Field-by-field merge semantics design and documentation (the load-bearing design work).
- End-to-end test that the original `drift_detection` bug is fixed and per-project override still works.

**Out of scope (separate follow-up tasks, not blockers):**
- **Python config readers.** `src/endless/config.py`, `event_bridge.py`, `register.py`, `reconcile.py`, plus several tests, all read the same JSON files directly. Python cannot use `go-cfgstore`. They keep working in this task but will diverge from Go semantics until a follow-up either reimplements matching semantics in Python or moves Python to call a Go shim. Documented as a known gap; file follow-up task.
- **`ConfigDir()` helpers** in `internal/monitor/db.go`, `cmd/endless-hook/claude.go`, `cmd/endless-channel/main.go`. These resolve `~/.config/endless/` for log/db file locations, not for reading user settings. Out of scope here; can migrate to `go-cfgstore`'s `CLIConfigDir()` later.
- **Schema versioning** (`RootConfigV1`) per `go-configuration.md` guidance. Not needed until the schema actually changes.

1. **`checks` merge granularity.** Granular per-key merge. Default rule for keys without a custom rule: project wins if set, else inherit global, else fall back to `defaultCheckEnabled(name)`.
2. **`tracking` layerability.** Layerable. Global may set a default; project overrides only when explicitly set. Empty/unset on the project side means inherit, not "off".

# E-957: General-purpose `task link`/`unlink` CLI

## Context

Endless task↔decision pairs and other cross-task relationships have become painfully common (E-957, E-958, E-975/E-976, E-977/E-978). Today only `block`/`unblock` and `replace` create typed relations, and the display layer surfaces only those two dep_types — every other linkage gets lost in description text, unlinkable and unqueryable.

E-958 (now confirmed) locks the vocabulary: `link` is the canonical CLI verb (the agent-instinctive choice; see `~/.claude/projects/-Users-mikeschinkel-Projects-endless/memory/feedback_cli_naming_agent_friction.md`). `block` and `replace` survive as thin shortcut wrappers. Six initial dep_types are frozen: `blocks/blocked_by`, `needs` (kept only as a transition synonym → migrated away), `replaces/replaced_by`, `implements/implemented_by`, `informs/informed_by`, `relates_to`.

This plan implements E-957's full punch list. Outcome: any task or decision can be linked to any other with a typed relationship; `task show` displays all relations grouped; `task add` and `decision add` accept at-creation flags; reverse lookup via `task list --related-to`; legacy `block`/`replace` continue to work.

## Decisions resolved up front

1. **Storage direction:** active voice. A row stores `source=actor, target=acted_upon, dep_type=<active_verb>`. So a row with `dep_type='blocks'` reads "source blocks target" — source is the blocker, target is the blocked task. Existing `needs` rows (stored as `source=blocked, target=blocker, dep_type='needs'`) get their source/target swapped AND the dep_type renamed to `'blocks'`. **This also fixes a latent bug in `replaces` rows** — `replace_task` (task_cmd.py) currently stores `source=old, target=new, dep_type='replaces'`, which reads literally as "old replaces new" but the comment and behavior treat it as "old replaced_by new". The label is active but the layout is passive — they disagree. Migration swaps source/target for existing `replaces` rows so the active label matches the layout going forward.

   *Why this over passive storage:* the CLI verb (`task block`, `task replace`), the stored dep_type (`'blocks'`, `'replaces'`), and the row layout all align. Active voice is what agents and humans reach for naturally; reading raw SQL says the same thing the verb implies. Worth the one-time migration cost.

2. **Canonical stored dep_types** (5 stored, all active voice; 4 inverse views computed): `blocks`, `implements`, `informs`, `replaces`, `relates_to` are stored. Their inverses `blocked_by`, `implemented_by`, `informed_by`, `replaced_by` are the same row queried with source/target swapped. `relates_to` is symmetric (no inverse name).
3. **`decision add --about` vs `--decides`:** two flags, two semantics. `--about <task-id>` → `dep_type=informs` (soft: decision provides context). `--decides <task-id>` → `dep_type=implements` with source=task, target=decision (hard: task implements this decision; equivalent to `implements` from the task side).
4. **Legacy CHECK constraint** in `db.py` (`CHECK (dep_type IN ('blocks', 'needs'))`) must be dropped from any DB that has it. SQLite has no `DROP CHECK`, so the migration uses table-rebuild (CREATE new, INSERT … SELECT, DROP, RENAME) inside a transaction. Migration is idempotent (detects CHECK in `sqlite_master.sql`).
5. **`add_item` returns the new id.** Cleaner than threading through the event payload. Only the CLI layer at cli.py currently ignores the return.
6. **`unlink` without `--as`:** when omitted, query all dep_types between the pair. Zero → "no relation" error. One → remove it. Multiple → error listing them and require `--as`. Never silent delete.
7. **Display order in `task show`:** fixed, action-priority descending, only render groups with rows: `blocked_by`, `blocks`, `implements`, `implemented_by`, `informs`, `informed_by`, `replaces`, `replaced_by`, `relates_to`.

## Context

E-995 establishes a first-class sandbox/fixture mechanism so that tests and verification work that mutate Endless state run against an isolated DB + event log, never the live system. Today there is no such primitive — every session reinvents one (E-787 Phase 5 used `.test-isolated/`, conftest.py uses ad-hoc XDG redirection, and the lack of a sandbox tempted raw-SQL bypass during E-979 cleanup, declined as E-993). E-995's plan is locked, with 7 confirmed decisions (E-1066, E-1068, E-1069, E-1070, E-1071, E-1072, plus storage layout in the plan body).

This task is Phase 1 of E-995 — the foundational Go binary that every other phase depends on. It exposes the sandbox CLI surface, owns provisioning + cleanup + orphan detection, and uses Go 1.26's `os.Root` for kernel-level write barrier on the sandbox dir. Deep clone (decision E-1071) is **deferred to a follow-up child task**: the binary accepts `--clone` and warns "not yet implemented", proceeding with an empty sandbox. This keeps Phase 1 focused on the CLI + lifecycle plumbing every later phase calls into.

## Worktree setup (auto-mode will run these on plan approval)

Work happens on a dedicated worktree per E-1074:

```bash
git -C /Users/mikeschinkel/Projects/endless worktree add -b task/1074-sandbox-go-binary \
    /Users/mikeschinkel/Projects/endless/.endless/worktrees/e-1074
cd /Users/mikeschinkel/Projects/endless/.endless/worktrees/e-1074
just go-work-init
```

`go.mod` has `replace ../go-pkgs/X` directives that only resolve from the main checkout. `just go-work-init` writes a per-checkout `go.work` (gitignored) with absolute paths so Go builds work inside the worktree. Without this, `just build` fails immediately. Broader strategy is open as E-1085.

`endless task start E-1074` and the `in_progress` status flip already ran on the main checkout per the user prompt — re-run inside the worktree if session registration is needed.

**Do NOT run `just install` from the worktree.** Editable `uv tool install -e .` would point the global Python tool at this worktree's source, which disappears when the worktree is dropped. Use `just build` only; binaries land in `./bin/` and are invoked via the explicit `./bin/endless-sandbox` path.

## Files to create

All paths relative to the worktree root:

- `cmd/endless-sandbox/main.go` — dispatcher: parse `os.Args[1]`, route to subcommand handlers, exit codes
- `cmd/endless-sandbox/sandbox.go` — `Sandbox` type, meta JSON read/write, provisioning, destroy, name generation, `os.Root` open
- `cmd/endless-sandbox/run.go` — `run` subcommand: provision → exec via `os/exec` → defer destroy → SIGINT/TERM/HUP handler triggers same cleanup
- `cmd/endless-sandbox/enter.go` — `enter` subcommand: provision-or-load named sandbox, fork `$SHELL` subshell with sandbox env (XDG_CONFIG_HOME, ENDLESS_SANDBOX, PATH preserved)
- `cmd/endless-sandbox/list.go` — walk cache dir, parse each meta, classify Live / In-use / Orphaned, render table
- `cmd/endless-sandbox/prune.go` — orphans-only filter, `--older-than DURATION` with 24h minimum (error below), print scope before acting
- `cmd/endless-sandbox/destroy.go` — explicit destroy by name (lookup meta, RemoveAll dir)
- `cmd/endless-sandbox/orphan.go` — `isAlive(pid)` via `syscall.Kill(pid, 0)` (ESRCH → dead, EPERM → alive); orphan classification helper shared by `list` and `prune`
- `cmd/endless-sandbox/sandbox_test.go` — table test proving `os.Root` blocks out-of-sandbox writes with EACCES

## Files to modify

- `internal/monitor/db.go` — add `CacheDir() string` parallel to existing `ConfigDir()`. Returns `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/endless` if set, else `$HOME/.cache/endless`. Used by `endless-sandbox` to compute `<CacheDir>/sandboxes/<name>/`. Reusing `ConfigDir`'s pattern keeps the helper next to its sibling.
- `Justfile` — add `go build -o bin/endless-sandbox ./cmd/endless-sandbox` to `build:`, `go:`, and the symlink line in `install:`. Three places, matching existing binaries.

## Reusable helpers (already exist — do not reinvent)

- `monitor.ConfigDir()` (`internal/monitor/db.go`) — XDG-aware config dir; pattern to mirror for the new `CacheDir()`.
- Signal handling pattern in `cmd/endless-channel/main.go` — `signal.Notify(sigCh, syscall.SIGTERM, syscall.SIGINT)` is the in-repo precedent; extend to add SIGHUP.
- `flag.NewFlagSet(name, flag.ExitOnError)` subcommand pattern from `cmd/endless-event/main.go` — copy this dispatch shape.

## CLI surface (final)

```
endless-sandbox run    [--clone] [--name N] [--keep] -- <cmd> [args...]
endless-sandbox enter  [--clone] <name>
endless-sandbox list
endless-sandbox prune  [--older-than DURATION]
endless-sandbox destroy <name>
```

Storage: `~/.cache/endless/sandboxes/<name>/` (XDG_CACHE_HOME-aware).

Meta file at `<sandbox>/.sandbox-meta.json`:
```json
{
  "created_at": "2026-05-01T12:00:00Z",
  "mode": "ephemeral" | "keep",
  "creator_pid": 12345,
  "name": "abc123ef"
}
```

### Behavioral decisions (judgment calls inside the prompt's latitude)

- **`--clone` is deferred.** Flag is accepted by `run` and `enter` but logs `"warning: --clone deep-copy not yet implemented (see E-NEW); sandbox starts empty"` and proceeds. A child task `Implement --clone deep-copy for endless-sandbox` will be filed via `endless task add` on plan approval (parent E-995, references E-1071). Phase 1 does not block on the deep-copy implementation.
- **`enter` always provisions as `mode=keep`.** Entering a sandbox implies a session you might exit and return to; ephemeral semantics don't fit. To dispose, use `destroy <name>` explicitly.
- **`run --name foo` collisions error.** If `foo` already exists, error with `"sandbox 'foo' already exists; use 'endless-sandbox destroy foo' first"`. Force-overwrite is not in scope.
- **List labels:**
  - **Live**: `mode=ephemeral` AND `creator_pid` alive (currently in-flight `run`)
  - **In-use**: `mode=keep` (intentionally persistent, regardless of pid state)
  - **Orphaned**: `mode=ephemeral` AND `creator_pid` dead (E-1068 startup warning will count these)
- **Random ephemeral names:** 8-char hex from `crypto/rand` (e.g. `a7f3c8d1`). Deterministic enough for `list` to display, random enough that two parallel ephemerals never collide.
- **Subshell for `enter`:** `exec.Command(os.Getenv("SHELL"))` with `cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<sandbox>", "ENDLESS_SANDBOX=<sandbox>")`. Stdin/stdout/stderr inherited. User runs commands; `exit` returns to parent. Per E-1072.
- **Cleanup ordering:** `run` registers `defer destroy()` and a goroutine listening on a signal channel that calls the same `destroy()` then `os.Exit(130)`. SIGKILL/crashes leave the sandbox on disk by design (E-1068/E-1069 orphan inspection).

## `os.Root` enforcement details

After creating the sandbox dir with regular `os.MkdirAll` (since the dir doesn't exist yet, can't be opened as a Root), call `os.OpenRoot(sandboxDir)`. Pass the `*os.Root` into provisioning code that writes `.sandbox-meta.json` (use `root.Create(".sandbox-meta.json")`) and any clone-data writes (when E-NEW lands). Destroy uses raw `os.RemoveAll(sandboxDir)` since it acts on the sandbox dir itself, not within it.

The `os.Root` test in `sandbox_test.go` will:
1. Provision a tmp sandbox via the same code path
2. Attempt `root.Create("../escape.txt")` → assert error contains "path escapes" or syscall returns EACCES
3. Attempt `root.OpenFile("/etc/passwd", os.O_RDONLY, 0)` → assert error
4. Confirm `root.Create("legit.txt")` succeeds

## Exit codes & output

- `run`: propagates child command's exit code; non-zero on provisioning failure
- `prune`: `0` even if nothing to prune; non-zero on flag errors (e.g. `--older-than 0s` → exit 1, stderr `"minimum --older-than is 24h"`)
- `list`: table to stdout: `NAME  MODE  STATE  AGE  SIZE  CREATOR_PID`. AGE in human-readable (`2h15m`); SIZE via `du`-equivalent walk
- `prune`: stderr scope line first (`"Pruning N orphaned ephemeral sandboxes older than 24h: a b c"`), then on success stdout `"Pruned: a b c"`. No-op message when zero matches.

## Out of scope (explicitly NOT in this task)

- `--clone` implementation (DB copy + per-project state walk + path rewrite) — child task `Implement --clone deep-copy for endless-sandbox` filed at plan approval
- Python `endless sandbox` CLI group (Phase 2, separate task already exists or will be filed)
- Binary-selection helper (Phase 3, E-1077)
- pytest fixture / `Sandbox` Python class (Phase 4)
- Startup orphan warning (Phase 5, E-1079) — this task only exposes `list` so Phase 5 has something to call
- Documentation (Phase 6)

## Verification

Run from inside the worktree, NOT after `just install`:

1. **Build:** `just build` — `bin/endless-sandbox` appears alongside other binaries
2. **Existing tests pass:** `just test` (Python) and `just test-go` (Go) — neither should regress; this is a new isolated binary
3. **Go test:** `go test ./cmd/endless-sandbox/...` — the `os.Root` EACCES test passes
4. **Smoke (sequential, all from the worktree):**
   - `./bin/endless-sandbox run -- echo hi` → prints `hi`; `~/.cache/endless/sandboxes/` is empty afterwards (ephemeral auto-destroy)
   - `./bin/endless-sandbox run --keep --name test1 -- echo hi` → exits 0; `./bin/endless-sandbox list` shows `test1  keep  in-use  …`
   - `./bin/endless-sandbox prune` → no-op message (no orphans yet)
   - `./bin/endless-sandbox prune --older-than 0s` → exits 1, stderr `"minimum --older-than is 24h"`
   - Orphan creation: `./bin/endless-sandbox run -- sleep 60 &` then `kill -9 $!` → `list` shows the ephemeral as Orphaned
   - `./bin/endless-sandbox destroy test1` → removes named sandbox; `list` no longer shows it
   - `./bin/endless-sandbox enter test2` (in a tmux pane or interactive shell) → forks subshell; `echo $ENDLESS_SANDBOX` shows path; `exit` returns to parent

## Endless task hygiene (on plan approval, before coding)

- File child task: `endless task add "Implement --clone deep-copy for endless-sandbox" --parent E-995` (references E-1071's deep-clone decision; this is what `--clone` will actually do once implemented)

## When done

- Both `just build` and `just test` pass cleanly on the worktree
- Commit on `task/1074-sandbox-go-binary` (do not merge to main)
- `endless task update E-1074 --status verify` (Mike sets `confirmed` after review)
- Report what was built and any deviations

# E-1130 — Skip endless-hook work when cwd is in a worktree but binary is the global one

## Context

E-998 ships a per-worktree `.claude/settings.json` so a Claude session inside a worktree fires `<worktree>/bin/endless-hook` instead of swapping the global `/usr/local/bin/endless-hook` symlink. E-1129 verified that Claude Code MERGES hook entries across user/project/local settings layers — does not replace. As a result, a session whose cwd is inside the worktree fires BOTH binaries for every event. State-mutating event handlers (`InitSession`, `ParseTranscript`, `SetProcess`, `RegisterTaskFile`, `EndSession`, …) execute twice for that session: duplicate DB rows, duplicate companion-file writes, duplicate task-context injection.

E-998's cross-session safety goal is intact (sessions outside the worktree still fire only the global), so this is a worktree-session-only side effect. The fix lives entirely in the global binary: when invoked from a cwd inside an endless-managed worktree that has its own `bin/endless-hook` (different file from the running binary), the global short-circuits before any state mutation. The worktree binary handles the event alone.

This is a developer-only concern — end users of endless never run two binaries on the same hook event.

## Approach

Add an early self-skip check in `cmd/endless-hook/claude.go` `runClaude`, immediately after `projectID` lookup (line 84) and BEFORE activity throttle/recording (line 87). All mutations — including `RecordActivity` — are guarded by the same skip.

### Skip logic (pseudocode)

```
if projectID == 0 || cwd == "" → no skip (run normally)
projectRoot ← monitor.ProjectPath(projectID)        // existing helper
worktreeRoot ← monitor.FindWorktreeRoot(cwd, projectRoot)  // existing helper
if worktreeRoot == "" → no skip (cwd is in main, foreign, or unrelated)

worktreeBin ← <worktreeRoot>/bin/endless-hook
worktreeStat ← os.Stat(worktreeBin)

if worktreeStat == nil and err is ErrNotExist:
    LOUD WARN: "cwd <cwd> is in worktree <worktreeRoot> but <worktreeBin> does not exist — running global as fallback. Run 'just build' in the worktree to enable the override."
    no skip (run normally)

if worktreeStat == nil and err is other:
    log error, no skip (run normally — never break the hook)

selfPath ← os.Executable()
selfStat ← os.Stat(selfPath)
if os.SameFile(selfStat, worktreeStat):
    no skip (I AM the worktree binary)

# We are the global, the worktree binary exists, we are inside the worktree:
log "deferring to <worktreeBin> (cwd is in worktree)"
return nil  // skip all event handling
```

### Why these choices

- **Identity check via `os.SameFile`.** Wraps the `(dev, ino)` comparison the user picked. Robust against the `/usr/local/bin/endless-hook` → `<main>/bin/endless-hook` symlink and any future symlink layout — `os.Stat` follows symlinks by default. No string/path matching.
- **Asymmetric design (only the global skips).** The worktree binary doesn't need to check anything — the global yielding is sufficient. This avoids a chicken-and-egg "should I run if the other is going to?" coordination.
- **Loud warn on missing worktree binary.** Per the configuration-must-loudly-complain principle: the hook still runs the global so the Claude session keeps working, but writes a clearly-marked message to both stderr and `<ConfigDir>/log/hook.log` (existing logger at `claude.go`). The user cannot miss a missed `just build`.
- **Skip BEFORE activity throttle.** The throttle would naturally dedup most concurrent fires, but not all (race within the throttle window) and the throttle has nothing to do with the architectural reason both fire. Skipping earlier is cleaner.
- **`os.Executable()` failure → no skip.** Defensive: if we can't determine our own path we run normally rather than break the hook.

## Critical files

- **`/Users/mikeschinkel/Projects/endless/cmd/endless-hook/claude.go`** — add skip helper, call it from `runClaude` between current line 84 and line 86. Also add an import for any new stdlib (none new — `os`, `filepath`, `log` already imported).
- **`/Users/mikeschinkel/Projects/endless/internal/monitor/worktree_lock.go`** — read-only: reuse `FindWorktreeRoot` (lines 220-245) verbatim.
- **`/Users/mikeschinkel/Projects/endless/internal/monitor/`** — read-only: reuse `ProjectPath` (already used by `handleWorktreeAdoption` at `claude.go`).

No new files. No package boundary changes. Skip helper lives as a private function in `claude.go` next to `handleWorktreeAdoption` (logically related).

## Tests

Two layers:

**Unit (Go).** New `cmd/endless-hook/claude_skip_test.go`. Cases:
- cwd outside any project → no skip
- cwd in main checkout (no worktree companion above it) → no skip
- cwd in worktree, worktree binary missing → no skip + warn log captured (assert via redirected log output)
- cwd in worktree, worktree binary exists, self == worktree binary → no skip
- cwd in worktree, worktree binary exists, self != worktree binary → SKIP

For the file-identity cases, the test creates a temp directory with `<wt>/.endless/worktree.json` (companion sentinel) and a `<wt>/bin/endless-hook` file. The "self" is faked by passing in the path used as `os.Executable` via a small seam (an injected function or a package-level var the test overrides). The exploration's logger writes to stderr+file via `log.SetOutput`; the test redirects `log.SetOutput` to a `bytes.Buffer` to assert the warn message.

**End-to-end (manual, recorded in commit).** From inside `.endless/worktrees/e-NNN/`:
1. `just build` → ensures `bin/endless-hook` exists.
2. `just claude-settings-init` → installs `.claude/settings.json`.
3. `endless task spawn <task>` → opens a tmux pane with Claude.
4. In that Claude session, type any prompt (fires UserPromptSubmit).
5. Tail `<ConfigDir>/log/hook.log` and grep for the new "deferring to" log line — should see exactly one (the global's deferral). The worktree binary's normal hook handling lines should also appear.
6. Query the events DB for rows with that session_id at the prompt timestamp — should be exactly one set, not two.
7. Spawn a second Claude session OUTSIDE any worktree (e.g., from `~/`). Confirm no "deferring to" line — global runs normally because cwd is not in a worktree.

## Out of scope

- Changing `claude-settings-init` to write `settings.local.json` instead — same merge rule applies, no benefit.
- Rolling back E-998 — sibling-session safety is the bigger win and stays.
- Detecting a "stale" worktree settings.json (settings file present but worktree gone) — the recipe is paired with worktree creation; mismatch only happens if someone hand-deletes `bin/` after running the recipe. The loud-warn covers it.
- Any change to the worktree binary's behavior — asymmetric design is intentional.

## Verification checklist before marking verify

- [ ] Unit tests pass: `go test ./cmd/endless-hook/...`
- [ ] All other tests pass: `just test` (Python), `go test ./internal/monitor/...`
- [ ] Manual E2E above produces exactly one "deferring to" log line per worktree-session event and exactly one set of DB rows.
- [ ] Manual E2E from main (no worktree) shows NO "deferring to" log lines and the global runs normally.
- [ ] Loud-warn case verified by deleting `<worktree>/bin/endless-hook` and re-firing: stderr and hook.log both contain the warning, hook still runs, Claude session is not broken.
- [ ] E-1130 plan attached to the task via `endless task update E-1130 --text .endless/plans/E-1130.md` and committed in the same commit.
- [ ] Branch lands on main; worktree removed; `just install` from main; status → `verify`.

## Repro from E-1450 land (2026-05-23): plan-file/DB divergence caused non-deterministic land-guard dirt

While landing E-1450, `just land` blocked at the worktree dirty-guard
(`worktree_cmd.py` `_guard_dirty_worktree`) reporting `.endless/plans/E-1450.md`
as "uncommitted user changes" — even though the file was committed on the task
branch and `git status --porcelain` in the worktree was empty (verified directly,
file tracked at HEAD with no diff).

State at the time of the failing land:
- `.endless/plans/E-1450.md` was committed on the branch, matched HEAD, clean.
- DB `tasks.text` for E-1450 DIVERGED from the committed file: the file had a
  post-approval "landing note" added by an editor, while the DB still held the
  pre-note version attached earlier via `task update --text`.

The land succeeded immediately after re-syncing the DB to the committed file
(`endless task update E-1450 --text <committed-file>`). Nothing else changed —
the worktree file was already committed/clean before and after; only the DB
content changed.

Mechanism NOT identified. Ruled out: no git hooks (core.hooksPath default,
.git/hooks empty); no land step writes the plan file (`land_worktree` never calls
the materializer at `task_cmd.py`); orphan-drop was a no-op (companion
base_branch="main", neither branch commit amendable); the endless-hook only reads
`~/.claude/plans`, never writes `.endless/plans`. That the exact path turning a
DB/file divergence into transient worktree dirt could not be found is itself
consistent with this task's premise that plan-storage is non-deterministic.

Design takeaway: the two-copy model (plan in DB `tasks.text` AND as a committed
`.endless/plans/E-NNN.md`) can drift, and the drift surfaces non-deterministically
at land time. Deterministic rules should make one copy the single source of truth
(or have land explicitly detect/reconcile divergence) rather than leaving
plan-storage state ambiguous. Related contested decision: 71 plan files are
currently tracked on main vs. E-1202's proposal to forbid them in main.
